Let $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma_1$ intersect at $A$ and $P$, $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma_2$ intersect at $B$ and $Q$, and $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma_3$ intersect at $C$ and $R$. (a) Prove that the circles $\Gamma_1$, $\Gamma_2$ and $\Gamma_3$ intersect in a common point. (b) Show that $PD$, $QE$ and $RF$ are concurrent.

ca.2008.0.5.reviewed_statement: A self-avoiding rook walk on a chessboard (a rectangular grid of unit squares) is a path traced by a sequence of moves parallel to an edge of the board from one unit square to another, such that each begins where the previous move ended and such that no move ever crosses a square that has previously been crossed, i.e., the rook's path is non-self-intersecting. Let $R(m, n)$ be the number of self-avoiding rook walks on an $m \times n$ ($m$ rows, $n$ columns) chessboard which begin at the lower-left corner and end at the upper-left corner. For example, $R(m, 1) = 1$ for all natural numbers $m$; $R(2, 2) = 2$; $R(3, 2) = 4$; $R(3, 3) = 11$. Find a formula for $R(3, n)$ for each natural number $n$.

ca.2010.0.1.reviewed_statement:
For a positive integer $n$, an $n$-staircase is a figure consisting of unit squares, with one square in the first row, two squares in the second row, and so on, up to $n$ squares in the $n$th row, such that all the left-most squares in each row are aligned vertically. For example, the $5$-staircase is shown below.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/canada_2010_p1_fig1.png

Let $f(n)$ denote the minimum number of square tiles required to tile the $n$-staircase, where the side lengths of the square tiles can be any positive integer. For example, $f(2) = 3$ and $f(4) = 7$.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/canada_2010_p1_fig2.png

ca.2010.0.3.reviewed_statement: Three speed skaters have a friendly "race" on a skating oval. They all start from the same point and skate in the same direction, but with different speeds that they maintain throughout the race. The slowest skater does 1 lap a minute, the fastest one does 3.14 laps a minute, and the middle one does $L$ laps a minute for some $1 < L < 3.14$. The race ends at the moment when all three skaters again come together to the same point on the oval (which may differ from the starting point). Find how many different choices for $L$ are there such that exactly 117 passings occur before the end of the race. (A passing is defined when one skater passes another one. The beginning and the end of the race when all three skaters are together are not counted as passings.)

ca.2010.0.4.reviewed_statement: Each vertex of a finite graph can be coloured either black or white. Initially all vertices are black. We are allowed to pick a vertex $P$ and change the colour of $P$ and all of its neighbours. Is it possible to change the colour of every vertex from black to white by a sequence of operations of this type? (A finite graph consists of a finite set of vertices and a finite set of edges between vertices. If there is an edge between vertex $A$ and vertex $B$, then $B$ is called a neighbour of $A$.)

ca.1969.0.1.reviewed_statement: Show that if $\dfrac{a_1}{b_1} = \dfrac{a_2}{b_2} = \dfrac{a_3}{b_3}$ and $p_1, p_2, p_3$ are not all zero, then $$\left(\frac{a_1}{b_1}\right)^n = \frac{p_1a_1^n + p_2a_2^n + p_3a_3^n}{p_1b_1^n + p_2b_2^n + p_3b_3^n}$$ for every positive integer $n$.
ca.1969.0.1.text: Editorial clarification: assume every displayed denominator is nonzero. The historical source omits this condition. For example, a1 = a2 = a3 = b1 = b2 = b3 = 1 and (p1, p2, p3) = (1, -1, 0) satisfy its stated assumptions but give 0/0 on the right. With the nonzero-denominator condition, the identity follows by substituting ai = r bi.

China-olympiad-problems.json.coverage_notes: Complete indexed six-problem papers: 1987–2026 (240 statements, 40 years). The nine restored AoPS papers (1995, 1996, 1998–2002, 2007–2008) were visually checked against the uploaded PDFs. Source errors and omitted tasks/domains were repaired only where documented in a separately inspected Chinese compilation or HKUST article; unresolved variants remain explicit. The 2008 P3 equality version is retained because the stronger magazine version fails for negative alpha. The 1994 and 1997 papers are restored from two inspected Chinese compilations, with the 1997 English-source variants documented. All forty indexed years in 1987–2026 have six statements. The 2017–2026 papers follow the existing AoPS edition-year convention: their Chinese calendar-year labels are 2016–2025. The AoPS 2026 paper was held on 26–27 November 2025. Sixty new English statements are compared with Chinese compilations or reproduced papers; ten statement-only PDFs and six extracted source figures are provided. This is not a claim that the calendar-2026 winter final has been held. No claim of complete historical coverage, independent solution review or universal official-source certification.

This checks the reproduced statements, not direct official hosting or independent solution certification. The bank retains the AoPS edition year; the physical paper is dated 2025.

cn.2026.1.2.reviewed_statement: A convex cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ has circumcenter $O$, circumradius $1$ and $\angle ABC<\angle BCD<90^\circ$. Let $P=BA\cap CD$ and $Q=AC\cap BD$. Suppose that some point $K$ on segment $BC$ satisfies that $P,A,K,D$ are concyclic and $KB\cdot KC=OP^2/2$. The perpendicular to $BC$ through $Q$ meets line $OP$ at $T$. Find all possible values of (a) $OP$ and (b) $TB+TC$.
cn.2026.1.2.scope: English statement compared with a visually inspected Chinese paper reproduction and the public AoPS reproduction. This checks the reproduced statements, not direct official hosting or independent solution certification. The bank retains the AoPS edition year; the physical paper is dated 2025.

cn.2026.1.3.reviewed_statement: Initially, $n$ red cards each carry $0$, and $n$ blue cards each carry $1$. A move chooses a red card with a smaller number than a blue card and replaces both numbers by their arithmetic mean. Find the smallest positive integer $n$ for which finitely many moves can make the sum of the numbers on the red cards greater than $100$.
cn.2026.1.3.scope: English statement compared with a visually inspected Chinese paper reproduction and the public AoPS reproduction. This checks the reproduced statements, not direct official hosting or independent solution certification. The bank retains the AoPS edition year; the physical paper is dated 2025.

cn.2026.2.4.reviewed_statement: There are thirty colors of cards, seventy cards of each color. Choose any seventy cards and arrange them in a stack. A move selects a card $X$ among the bottom twenty whose color is absent from the top fifty, selects a card $Y$ among the top fifty whose color occurs there at least twice, and moves $X$ immediately above $Y$. Repeat until no eligible $X$ remains. Prove that every sequence of moves terminates, and find the maximum possible number of moves over all initial stacks and choices.
cn.2026.2.4.scope: English statement compared with a visually inspected Chinese paper reproduction and the public AoPS reproduction. This checks the reproduced statements, not direct official hosting or independent solution certification. The bank retains the AoPS edition year; the physical paper is dated 2025.

cn.2026.2.5.reviewed_statement: Find all real numbers $\lambda$ for which there exists $N>0$ such that, for every integer $n\ge N$ and all nonnegative real numbers $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ with sum $1$, $$\left(\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}x_ix_j\right)^2\le\lambda\sum_{1\le i<j<k\le n}x_ix_jx_k+\frac1n\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}(x_i-x_j)^2.$$
cn.2026.2.5.scope: English statement compared with a visually inspected Chinese paper reproduction and the public AoPS reproduction. This checks the reproduced statements, not direct official hosting or independent solution certification. The bank retains the AoPS edition year; the physical paper is dated 2025.

cn.2026.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $n\ge3$ be odd and satisfy $\gcd(p-1,n)=1$ for every prime divisor $p$ of $n$. Count the triples $(a,b,c)\in\{1,2,\ldots,n\}^3$ such that $\gcd(a,b,c,n)=1$ and there exists a permutation $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ of $1,\ldots,n$ with $$ax_{k+2}+bx_{k+1}+cx_k\equiv0\pmod n$$ for every $1\le k\le n$, where indices are cyclic.
cn.2026.2.6.scope: English statement compared with a visually inspected Chinese paper reproduction and the public AoPS reproduction. This checks the reproduced statements, not direct official hosting or independent solution certification. The bank retains the AoPS edition year; the physical paper is dated 2025.

cn.2010.1.3.reviewed_statement: Complex numbers $a,b,c$ satisfy $|az^2+bz+c|\le1$ for every complex number $z$ with $|z|\le1$. Find the maximum possible value of $|bc|$.
cn.2010.1.3.text: Editorial correction: the retrieved book statement prints |az²+bz+c| ≥ 1, while its entire solution uses ≤ 1 and constructs a finite maximum under that upper bound. This record explicitly uses ≤ 1; it is not a literal transcription of the erroneous line. Independent original-paper confirmation remains pending.

cn.2010.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $n\ge3$. Cards are distributed among $n+1$ piles $A_1,\ldots,A_n,O$, with cyclic indices $A_0=A_n$ and $A_{n+1}=A_1$. Two moves are allowed: (1) if $A_i$ has at least three cards, remove three from it and add one to each of $A_{i-1},A_{i+1},O$; (2) if $O$ has at least $n$ cards, remove $n$ from it and add one to each $A_i$. Prove that if the total number of cards is at least $n^2+3n+1$, a finite sequence of moves can leave at least $n+1$ cards in every pile.
cn.2010.2.5.text: Source numbering discrepancy: the fifth problem is labelled 4 again in the retrieved reproduction. It is stored as problem 5 according to its position after second-day problem 4 and before problem 6.

cn.2010.1.1.reviewed_statement:
Two circles $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$ intersect at $A,B$. A line through $B$ meets them again at $C,D$, respectively; another line through $B$ meets them again at $E,F$, respectively. Line $CF$ meets $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$ again at $P,Q$, respectively. Let $M,N$ be the midpoints of arcs $PB,QB$, respectively, as in the figure. If $CD=EF$, prove that $C,F,M,N$ are concyclic.
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/china_2010_p1_fig.png
cn.2010.1.1.text: Source arc convention: the printed text does not specify which of the two arcs PB and QB is intended. The original statement figure is retained to show its configuration; no extra arc condition has been invented.

cn.2011.1.2.reviewed_statement:
In the configuration shown, $D$ is the midpoint of arc $BC$ of the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. Point $X$ lies on arc $BD$, $E$ is the midpoint of arc $AX$, and $S$ lies on arc $AC$. Lines $SD,BC$ meet at $R$, and lines $SE,AX$ meet at $T$. If $RT\parallel DE$, prove that the incentre of triangle $ABC$ lies on line $RT$.
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/china_2011_p2_fig.png
cn.2011.1.2.text: Source figure convention: the arcs and point positions follow the reproduced figure. The faithful crop also retains auxiliary labels I, J and K printed in that source figure; they introduce no additional assumptions.

cn.2014.1.1.reviewed_statement:
Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB>AC$. Its internal angle bisector from $A$ meets $BC$ at $D$. Points $E,F$ lie on sides $AB,AC$, respectively, and $B,C,F,E$ are concyclic. Prove that the circumcentre of triangle $DEF$ is the incentre of triangle $ABC$ if and only if $BE+CF=BC$.
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/china_2014_p1_fig.png
cn.2014.1.1.text: Year convention: this six-problem paper was held in Nanjing on 21–22 December 2013. The coach-authored source labels it 2013, while the English AoPS archive indexes the same paper as China National Olympiad 2014 (collection 5237). The bank retains the existing 2014 edition convention; this does not assert an examination date in calendar 2014.

cn.2015.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $A,B,D,E,F,C$ be six points on a circle, in that order, with $AB=AC$. Define $P=AD\cap BE$, $R=AF\cap CE$, $Q=BF\cap CD$, $S=AD\cap BF$, and $T=AF\cap CD$. Let $K$ lie on $ST$ and satisfy $\angle QKS=\angle ECA$. Prove that $$\frac{SK}{KT}=\frac{PQ}{QR}.$$
cn.2015.1.2.text: Source configuration convention: the AoPS compilation says K lies on ST without distinguishing the segment from its supporting line; it supplies no diagram or explicit exclusions for degenerate intersections. The source wording is retained pending primary-source comparison.

cn.2016.1.2.reviewed_statement: In triangle $AEF$, points $B,D$ lie on segments $AE,AF$, respectively, and $ED$ and $FB$ meet at $C$. Points $K,L,M,N$ lie on segments $AB,BC,CD,DA$, respectively, and satisfy $$\frac{AK}{KB}=\frac{AD}{BC},\quad\frac{BL}{LC}=\frac{BA}{CD},\quad\frac{CM}{MD}=\frac{CB}{DA},\quad\frac{DN}{NA}=\frac{DC}{AB}.$$ The incircle of triangle $AEF$ touches $AE,AF$ at $S,T$, respectively; the incircle of triangle $CEF$ touches $CE,CF$ at $U,V$, respectively. Prove that if $K,L,M,N$ are concyclic, then $S,T,U,V$ are concyclic.
cn.2016.1.2.text: Notation expansion: the AoPS statement specifies AK/KB = AD/BC and “its cyclic equivalents”. The other three ratios are displayed explicitly by cycling A, B, C, D. No original figure is present in the uploaded PDF.

cn.2016.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $p$ be an odd prime, and let $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_p$ be integers. Prove that the following conditions are equivalent: (1) There is a polynomial $P(x)$ of degree at most $(p-1)/2$ such that $P(i)\equiv a_i\pmod p$ for $1\le i\le p$. (2) For every natural number $d\le(p-1)/2$, $$\sum_{i=1}^{p}(a_{i+d}-a_i)^2\equiv0\pmod p,$$ where subscripts are interpreted modulo $p$.
cn.2016.1.3.text: Source domain omission: the AoPS compilation does not explicitly state the coefficient domain of P(x). Its wording is retained; an integer-coefficient or finite-field formulation needs confirmation against an original contest source.

cn.2016.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $G$ be a complete directed graph on $100$ vertices such that for any two vertices $x,y$ there is a directed path from $x$ to $y$. (a) Prove that there is an integer $m$ such that for any two vertices $x,y$ there is a directed path of length $m$ from $x$ to $y$; vertices may be repeated along a path. (b) For each such graph $G$, let $m(G)$ be the smallest possible $m$ in part (a). Find the minimum value of $m(G)$ over all such graphs.
cn.2016.2.6.text: Source convention and objective: the AoPS compilation says “complete directed graph” without explicitly defining the orientation convention. It asks for the minimum, not the maximum, of m(G) in part (b). Both are retained literally pending comparison with the original contest paper.

cn.1988.1.2.reviewed_statement: Two concentric circles have radii $r$ and $2r$. A convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in the smaller circle. The extensions of $AB,BC,CD,DA$ meet the larger circle at $C_1,D_1,A_1,B_1$, respectively. (a) Prove that the perimeter of $A_1B_1C_1D_1$ is at least twice that of $ABCD$. (b) Determine when equality holds.
cn.1988.1.2.text: Source extension convention: the book says extensions of the four sides but does not explicitly select between the two intersections of each supporting line with the larger circle. No statement figure is printed. The wording is retained pending original-paper comparison.

cn.1988.2.4.reviewed_statement: (a) Let $a_1,a_2,a_3>0$ satisfy $$(a_1^2+a_2^2+a_3^2)^2>2(a_1^4+a_2^4+a_3^4).$$ Prove that they are the side lengths of a triangle. (b) Let $n>3$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_n>0$ satisfy $$\left(\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2\right)^2>(n-1)\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^4.$$ Prove that any three with distinct indices are the side lengths of a triangle.
cn.1988.2.4.text: Editorial correction: part (b) on printed page 31 omits the outer square on the sum of squares. The bank restores that square, as explicitly used in the book's inductive proof on printed page 114 (scan page 121). The conclusion is expressed for distinct indices, as in that proof. Original-paper confirmation remains pending.

cn.1989.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ be positive real numbers with $x_1+\cdots+x_n=1$. Prove that $$\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{x_i}{\sqrt{1-x_i}}\ge\frac{\sum_{i=1}^n\sqrt{x_i}}{\sqrt{n-1}}.$$
cn.1989.1.2.text: Source domain omission: the book does not explicitly require n ≥ 2, although its formula is undefined for n = 1. The positive-variable sum condition and printed formula are preserved; apply only where the displayed denominators are defined.

cn.1989.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $S=(1,\infty)$. Determine all functions $f:S\to S$ such that $$f(x^my^n)\le f(x)^{1/(4m)}f(y)^{1/(4n)}$$ for all real $x,y>1$ and $m,n>0$.
cn.1989.2.6.text: Source exponent transcription: the scan prints 1/(4m) and 1/(4n) as the two exponents. They are retained literally; no replacement based on a presumed intended problem has been made.

cn.1990.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with $AB$ not parallel to $CD$. A circle through $A,B$ is tangent to $CD$ at $P$, and a circle through $C,D$ is tangent to $AB$ at $Q$. Prove that the common chord of the circles bisects $PQ$ if and only if $AD\parallel BC$.
cn.1990.1.1.text: Source existence omission: the statement refers to a common chord without separately assuming that the circles have two distinct intersections. No extra intersection condition has been silently added.

cn.1990.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ satisfy $$f(x)f(y)\le y^2f(x/2)+x^2f(y/2)$$ for all $x\ge y>0$, and suppose $|f(x)|\le M$ for $0\le x\le1$, where $M$ is a fixed constant. Prove that $f(x)\le x^2$.
cn.1990.1.3.text: Unresolved source endpoint error: the hypothesis constrains f only through positive x and y, while the declared domain includes zero. The printed conclusion has no positive-x restriction. For example f(x)=0 for x>0 and f(0)=1 satisfies the hypotheses but fails the conclusion at zero. The record preserves the printed formulation; use its conclusion only for x>0 pending original-paper confirmation.

cn.1993.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be an odd positive integer. Prove that there are integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n,b_1,\ldots,b_n$ such that, for every integer $k$ with $0\le k<n$, the following $3n$ integers are pairwise incongruent modulo $3n$: $$a_i+a_{i+1},\qquad a_i+b_i,\qquad b_i+b_{i+k}\qquad(1\le i\le n),$$ with subscripts interpreted modulo $n$.
cn.1993.1.1.text: Editorial correction: the printed statement on page 52 gives the third family as a_i+b_(i+k). The book's construction and proof on pages 181–182 (scan pages 188–189) instead use b_i+b_(i+k). The bank adopts the latter explicitly: at k=0 the printed third family would duplicate the second family. Original-paper confirmation remains pending.

cn.1993.1.3.reviewed_statement: Two concentric circles have radii $R<R_1$. Quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in the smaller circle and $A_1B_1C_1D_1$ in the larger, with $A_1,B_1,C_1,D_1$ on the extensions of $CD,DA,AB,BC$, respectively. Prove that $$\frac{[A_1B_1C_1D_1]}{[ABCD]}\ge\frac{R_1^2}{R^2},$$ where $[P]$ denotes the area of polygon $P$.
cn.1993.1.3.text: Source configuration omission: the book does not explicitly state convexity or select the direction of each side extension. Its wording is retained; no statement figure is printed and no unverified diagram has been added.

cn.1993.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $S$ be a set of $1993$ nonzero vectors in the plane. Prove that $S$ can be partitioned into nonempty subsets such that the angle between every vector in a subset and the sum of the vectors of that subset is at most $90^\circ$, while the angle between the vector sums of any two subsets is greater than $90^\circ$.
cn.1993.2.4.text: Source resultant convention: the source discusses angles to subset sums without explicitly requiring those sums to be nonzero. The intended angle condition presupposes nonzero resultant vectors; no separate original-paper confirmation is claimed.

cn.1995.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ satisfy $f(1)=1$ and, for every $n\in\mathbb N$, $$3f(n)f(2n+1)=f(2n)(1+3f(n)),\qquad f(2n)<6f(n).$$ Find all solutions of $f(k)+f(l)=293$ with $k<l$. Here $\mathbb N$ denotes the natural numbers.
cn.1995.1.2.text: Natural-number convention: the AoPS PDF does not state whether zero is included. The recurrence forces f(0)=0 if zero is included; the Chinese compilation uses the same natural-number wording. No convention has been silently selected.

cn.1995.1.3.reviewed_statement: Find the minimum value of $$\sum_{i=1}^{10}\sum_{j=1}^{10}\sum_{k=1}^{10}\left|k(x+y-10i)(3x-6y-36j)(19x+95y-95k)\right|,$$ where $x,y$ are real numbers.
cn.1995.1.3.text: Documented source correction: AoPS restricts x,y to integers, while the Chinese contest-and-solution compilation, scan page 31 (printed 30), states arbitrary real numbers. The bank restores the real-variable domain. No official original-paper certification is claimed.

cn.1995.2.4.reviewed_statement: Four spheres have radii $2,2,3,3$, respectively, and each is externally tangent to the other three. A further sphere is externally tangent to all four. Determine its radius.
cn.1995.2.4.text: Source convention: the Chinese compilation calls the further sphere a small sphere; AoPS omits that qualifier. The external-tangency wording is retained; no diagram is printed in the uploaded statement PDF.

cn.1995.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{10}$ be pairwise distinct natural numbers whose sum is $1995$. Find the minimum value of $$a_1a_2+a_2a_3+\cdots+a_9a_{10}+a_{10}a_1.$$
cn.1995.2.5.text: Natural-number convention: AoPS and the Chinese contest-and-solution compilation say natural numbers without explicitly defining whether zero is admitted. The Chinese retyped compilation instead says positive integers. The uploaded AoPS wording is retained; this discrepancy remains unresolved.

cn.1996.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with orthocentre $H$. The tangents from $A$ to the circle with diameter $BC$ touch it at $P,Q$. Prove that $H,P,Q$ are collinear.
cn.1996.1.1.text: Documented source correction: the acute-triangle hypothesis omitted by AoPS is restored from the Chinese contest-and-solution compilation, scan page 34. It ensures that the two real tangents in the configuration exist.

cn.1996.2.4.reviewed_statement: Eight singers take part in a festival. An organizer schedules $m$ concerts, with four singers performing at each concert. Every pair of singers must perform together the same number of times. Find a schedule minimizing $m$.
cn.1996.2.4.text: Source omission: both compilations omit an explicit positive requirement on m or on the common number of joint appearances. A nonempty festival schedule is presupposed; allowing zero concerts gives a trivial schedule. No unconfirmed condition was silently added.

cn.1999.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $a$ be real. Define polynomials $f_n(x)$ by $f_0(x)=1$ and $$f_{n+1}(x)=xf_n(x)+f_n(ax)\qquad(n\ge0).$$ (a) Prove that $f_n(x)=x^nf_n(x^{-1})$ for every nonnegative integer $n$. (b) Find an explicit expression for $f_n(x)$.
cn.1999.1.2.text: Reciprocal-domain convention: part (a) uses x inverse and therefore applies for x nonzero, or as a polynomial identity after clearing the reciprocal. The source does not state that restriction separately.

cn.2000.2.4.reviewed_statement: For an ordered real $n$-tuple $A=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$, where $n\ge2$, define $b_k=\max\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}$ and $B=(b_1,\ldots,b_n)$. Call $B$ the innovated tuple of $A$, and call the number of distinct entries of $B$ the innovated degree of $A$. Among all permutations of $1,2,\ldots,n$ whose innovated degree is $2$, find the arithmetic mean of their first entries.
cn.2000.2.4.text: Source variant: AoPS and the Chinese contest-and-solution compilation (scan page 52) ask for the mean of the first entry. The separate Chinese retyped compilation asks for every entry. The uploaded AoPS task is retained.

cn.2000.2.5.reviewed_statement: Find all positive integers $n$ for which there exist a positive integer $k$ and integers $n_1,\ldots,n_k>3$ satisfying $$n=n_1n_2\cdots n_k=2^{\frac{(n_1-1)(n_2-1)\cdots(n_k-1)}{2^k}}-1.$$
cn.2000.2.5.text: Documented source correction: the Chinese contest-and-solution compilation, scan page 53, requires every n_i to be greater than 3, whereas AoPS prints greater than or equal to 3. The strict condition is restored. The denominator in the exponent is 2^k, verified visually in both sources.

cn.2001.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $\sqrt2<a<2$. Let $ABCD$ be a convex cyclic quadrilateral with its circumcentre in its interior. Its circumcircle $\omega$ has radius $1$, and its longest and shortest sides have lengths $a$ and $\sqrt{4-a^2}$, respectively. The tangents to $\omega$ at $A,B,C,D$ are $L_A,L_B,L_C,L_D$. Put $A\prime=L_A\cap L_B$, $B\prime=L_B\cap L_C$, $C\prime=L_C\cap L_D$, $D\prime=L_D\cap L_A$. Determine the maximum and minimum possible values of $$\frac{S_{A\prime B\prime C\prime D\prime}}{S_{ABCD}}.$$
cn.2001.1.1.text: Documented task restoration: AoPS asks only for the minimum ratio. The Chinese contest-and-solution compilation, scan page 54, asks for both the maximum and minimum; both tasks are restored.

cn.2001.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $a=2001$, and let $A$ consist of all pairs of positive integers $(m,n)$ satisfying $$m<2a,\qquad 2n\mid(2am-m^2+n^2),\qquad n^2-m^2+2mn\le2a(n-m).$$ For $(m,n)\in A$, define $$f(m,n)=\frac{2am-m^2-mn}{n}.$$ Determine the maximum and minimum values of $f$.
cn.2001.2.6.text: Documented domain restoration: AoPS allows arbitrary integer pairs with n nonzero. The Chinese contest-and-solution compilation, scan page 56, requires positive integer pairs. Positivity is restored rather than retaining an unbounded altered problem.

cn.2002.1.1.reviewed_statement: Triangle $ABC$ has side lengths $a=BC$, $b=CA$, $c=AB$, with $b<c$. Its internal angle bisector $AD$ meets $BC$ at $D$. (1) Find a necessary and sufficient condition, expressed in terms of $\angle A,\angle B,\angle C$, for the existence of points $E,F$ in the interiors of $AB,AC$, respectively, such that $BE=CF$ and $\angle BDE=\angle CDF$. (2) When such points exist, express $BE$ in terms of $a,b,c$.
cn.2002.1.1.text: Documented source correction: undefined angle NDE in AoPS is BDE in the Chinese contest-and-solution compilation, scan page 58, and the Chinese retyped compilation, scan page 33. Both also require E,F strictly inside the side segments. These conditions are restored explicitly.

cn.2002.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let polynomials $p_n(x)$ satisfy $$p_1(x)=x^2-1,\qquad p_2(x)=2x(x^2-1),$$ and $$p_{n+1}(x)p_{n-1}(x)=p_n(x)^2-(x^2-1)^2\qquad(n\ge2).$$ Let $s_n$ be the sum of the absolute values of the coefficients of $p_n(x)$. For each $n$, find a nonnegative integer $k_n$ such that $2^{-k_n}s_n$ is odd.
cn.2002.1.2.text: Typographical repair: the AoPS recurrence has an unmatched opening parenthesis before p_n(x)^2. The balanced recurrence is confirmed on scan page 58 of the Chinese contest-and-solution compilation.

cn.2002.2.4.reviewed_statement: For four distinct points $P_1,P_2,P_3,P_4$ in the plane, find the minimum possible value of $$\frac{\sum_{1\le i<j\le4}P_iP_j}{\min_{1\le i<j\le4}P_iP_j}.$$
cn.2002.2.4.text: Documented domain restoration: the distinctness of the four points, omitted by AoPS and needed for the denominator, is explicit in the Chinese retyped compilation, scan page 34.

cn.2002.2.5.reviewed_statement: A point of the plane is called good if both its coordinates are rational. Prove that the good points can be partitioned into three sets such that: (1) the interior of every circle whose centre is good contains a point from each set; (2) no three collinear points belong to three different sets.
cn.2002.2.5.text: Circle-interior clarification: scan page 61 of the Chinese contest-and-solution compilation says every circle centered at a rational point contains a point of each of the three sets in its interior. This means one point from each set, not exactly three points per set and not points on the circumference.

cn.2007.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $a_1,\ldots,a_{11}$ be pairwise distinct positive integers with sum less than $2007$. Begin with the ordered sequence $S=(1,2,\ldots,2007)$. An operation consists of $22$ successive steps: at step $i$, choose an entry $x$ of the current sequence and replace it with $x+a_i$ if $1\le i\le11$, or with $x-a_{i-11}$ if $12\le i\le22$. Call the operation odd or even if its final sequence is, respectively, an odd or even permutation of $1,\ldots,2007$. Which is larger, the number of odd operations or the number of even operations, and by how much? A permutation $(x_1,\ldots,x_{2007})$ is even when $\prod_{i>j}(x_i-x_j)>0$, and odd otherwise.
cn.2007.1.3.text: Documented task correction: AoPS asks for the number of odd operations versus even permutations, although both classes are defined as operations. The Chinese magazine statement embedded on scan page 91 of the contest-and-solution compilation compares even and odd operation groups; the bank uses that comparison. The product definition of parity from AoPS is retained.

cn.2007.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $O,I$ be the circumcentre and incentre of triangle $ABC$. Its incircle touches $BC,CA,AB$ at $D,E,F$, respectively. Lines $FD,ED$ meet $CA,AB$ at $P,Q$, respectively. Let $M,N$ be the midpoints of $PE,QF$. Prove that $OI\perp MN$.
cn.2007.2.4.text: Source configuration omission: the sources do not explicitly exclude coincident incenter and circumcenter or parallel defining lines. The displayed construction must exist and the perpendicularity assertion presupposes a defined line OI; no unverified exclusions were added.

cn.2007.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $(a_n)_{n\ge1}$ be a bounded sequence satisfying $$a_n<\sum_{k=n}^{2n+2006}\frac{a_k}{k+1}+\frac1{2n+2007}\qquad(n=1,2,3,\ldots).$$ Prove that $a_n<1/n$ for every positive integer $n$.
cn.2007.2.5.text: Documented source correction: AoPS prints the undefined lower summation index k=a. The Chinese magazine statement on scan page 91 and Mathematical Excalibur 18(3), page 1, both give k=n and a strict inequality. The bank restores k=n. A separate retyped Chinese compilation incorrectly uses equality.

cn.2007.2.6.reviewed_statement: Find the smallest integer $n\ge9$ such that, for any $n$ integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, not necessarily distinct, there are indices $1\le i_1<\cdots<i_9\le n$ and coefficients $b_1,\ldots,b_9\in\{4,7\}$ for which $$b_1a_{i_1}+b_2a_{i_2}+\cdots+b_9a_{i_9}$$ is divisible by $9$.
cn.2007.2.6.text: Documented task and domain restoration: AoPS says find a number and does not specify that the a_i are integers. The Chinese magazine statement on scan page 91 requires the smallest integer n at least 9, arbitrary integer a_i, and coefficients in {4,7}. Those omitted conditions are restored.

cn.2008.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be an acute scalene triangle with circumcentre $O$. Let $A\prime$ lie on the extension of segment $AO$ such that $\angle BA\prime A=\angle CA\prime A$. Let $A_1,A_2$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $A\prime$ to $AC,AB$, respectively, and let $H_A$ be the foot of the perpendicular from $A$ to $BC$. Let $R_A$ be the circumradius of $H_AA_1A_2$, and define $R_B,R_C$ cyclically. Prove that $$\frac1{R_A}+\frac1{R_B}+\frac1{R_C}=\frac2R,$$ where $R$ is the circumradius of $ABC$.
cn.2008.1.1.text: Documented hypothesis restoration: the Chinese magazine statement on scan page 95 requires an acute scalene triangle, while AoPS omits acute. Its A_1,A_2 projection labels are also adopted; interchanging those two labels does not change the circumradius.

cn.2008.1.2.reviewed_statement: For an integer $n\ge3$, prove that $X=\{1,2,\ldots,n^2-n\}$ can be partitioned into two nonempty sets such that neither contains $n$ elements $a_1<\cdots<a_n$ satisfying $$a_k\le\frac{a_{k-1}+a_{k+1}}2\qquad(2\le k\le n-1).$$
cn.2008.1.2.text: Documented detail restoration: the Chinese magazine statement on scan page 95 explicitly requires both parts of the partition to be nonempty; AoPS omits nonempty.

cn.2008.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer and let real numbers $x_1\le\cdots\le x_n$ and $y_1\ge\cdots\ge y_n$ satisfy $$\sum_{i=1}^n ix_i=\sum_{i=1}^n iy_i.$$ Prove that, for every real $\alpha$, $$\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\lfloor i\alpha\rfloor\ge\sum_{i=1}^n y_i\lfloor i\alpha\rfloor.$$ Here $\lfloor\beta\rfloor$ is the greatest integer not exceeding $\beta$.
cn.2008.1.3.text: Unresolved source variant: AoPS assumes equal weighted sums and allows every real alpha. The Chinese magazine instead prints a greater-than-or-equal hypothesis with every real alpha, which is false as stated: n=1, x_1=1, y_1=0, alpha=-1 gives -1 >= 0. The bank retains the consistent equality version of the uploaded AoPS PDF; original-paper confirmation remains pending.

cn.2008.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $A$ be an infinite subset of the positive integers, and let $n>1$ be a fixed integer. Suppose that, for every prime $p$ not dividing $n$, infinitely many elements of $A$ are not divisible by $p$. Prove that, for every integer $m>1$ with $\gcd(m,n)=1$, there is a finite set of distinct elements of $A$ whose sum is congruent to $1$ modulo $m$ and to $0$ modulo $n$.
cn.2008.2.4.text: Documented domain restoration: the Chinese magazine statement on scan page 95 specifies n>1, positive integer elements and finitely many distinct elements in the resulting sum. These conditions omitted or abbreviated by AoPS are restored.

cn.2008.2.5.reviewed_statement: Find the smallest integer $n$ such that every coloring of the vertices of a regular $n$-gon with red, yellow or blue contains four vertices of the same color forming an isosceles trapezoid. Here an isosceles trapezoid has one pair of parallel sides and a pair of equal nonparallel sides; rectangles are excluded.
cn.2008.2.5.text: Documented trapezoid convention: the Chinese magazine statement on scan page 95 explicitly defines an isosceles trapezoid as having one pair of parallel sides and equal nonparallel sides. Thus rectangles are excluded. This definition is restored; it affects the task.

cn.2008.2.6.reviewed_statement: Find all triples $(p,q,n)$ satisfying $$q^{n+2}\equiv3^{n+2}\pmod{p^n},\qquad p^{n+2}\equiv3^{n+2}\pmod{q^n},$$ where $p,q$ are odd primes and $n$ is an integer greater than $1$.
cn.2008.2.6.text: Documented domain restoration: the Chinese magazine statement on scan page 95 requires n>1; AoPS only says n is positive. The original magazine domain is restored.

cn.1997.1.1.reviewed_statement: Real numbers $x_1,x_2,\ldots,x_{1997}$ satisfy $$-\frac1{\sqrt3}\le x_i\le\sqrt3\quad(1\le i\le1997),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^{1997}x_i=-318\sqrt3.$$ Find the maximum value of $$\sum_{i=1}^{1997}x_i^{12}$$ and justify your answer.
cn.1997.1.1.text: Source correction: the English 1996–1997 collection misprints the last exponent as 1/2. Both inspected Chinese compilations print the twelfth power for every variable; this consistent version is retained.

cn.1997.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $A=\{1,2,\ldots,17\}$ and let $f:A\to A$ be a bijection. Define $f^{[1]}=f$ and $f^{[k+1]}=f\circ f^{[k]}$ for positive integers $k$. Suppose there is a positive integer $M$ such that, for every $1\le m<M$ and $1\le i\le16$, $$f^{[m]}(i+1)-f^{[m]}(i)\not\equiv\pm1\pmod{17},\qquad f^{[m]}(1)-f^{[m]}(17)\not\equiv\pm1\pmod{17},$$ whereas $$f^{[M]}(i+1)-f^{[M]}(i)\equiv\pm1\pmod{17}\quad(1\le i\le16),\qquad f^{[M]}(1)-f^{[M]}(17)\equiv\pm1\pmod{17}.$$ Find the largest possible $M$ over all such bijections, and prove your answer.
cn.1997.2.5.text: The English collection lists i=1,...,16 and defines an eighteenth entry but does not explicitly print the wraparound difference. Both Chinese compilations explicitly include the difference between the images of 1 and 17. The bank retains this complete cyclic condition, with positive iteration indices.

cn.1997.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ be a sequence of nonnegative real numbers satisfying $$a_{n+m}\le a_n+a_m$$ for all positive integers $m,n$. Prove that, whenever $n\ge m\ge1$, $$a_n\le ma_1+\left(\frac nm-1\right)a_m.$$
cn.1997.2.6.text: Source-domain variant: the English collection restricts the sequence to nonnegative integers. Both inspected Chinese compilations say a nonnegative sequence without an integrality restriction. The bank renders this as nonnegative real terms; the bound is valid for that domain.

cn.2017.1.1.text: The inspected Chinese compilation explicitly requires eventual integer terms divisible by u_n; the shorter AoPS transcription omits the integer-term wording. The full condition is retained.
cn.2017.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,c$ be real numbers. Define $u_0=u_1=1$, $u_n=2u_{n-1}-3u_{n-2}$ for $n\ge2$, and $v_0=a$, $v_1=b$, $v_2=c$, $v_n=v_{n-1}-3v_{n-2}+27v_{n-3}$ for $n\ge3$. Suppose that for some positive integer $N$, every $v_n$ with $n\ge N$ is an integer divisible by $u_n$. Prove that $3a=2b+c$.

cn.2017.1.2.text: The inspected Chinese statement includes AB>AC, omitted in the AoPS transcription. It also describes P,Q as a diameter through I; the full Chinese condition is retained.
cn.2017.1.2.reviewed_statement:
Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle with $AB>AC$, circumcenter $O$ and incenter $I$. Its incircle touches $BC$ at $D$. The tangents to its circumcircle at $B$ and $C$ meet at $L$. Let $X=AO\cap BC$ and let $Y$ be the foot of the altitude from $A$ to $BC$. Let $P,Q$ be the endpoints of the diameter of the circumcircle passing through $I$. Prove that $A,D,L$ are collinear if and only if $P,X,Y,Q$ are concyclic.

cn.2020.1.1.text: The compilation prints |a_i|-|a_{i+1}|<=1, whereas AoPS prints |a_i-a_{i+1}|<=1. The latter version is retained: the former would allow arbitrarily large alternating terms and invalidate the finite maximum task.
cn.2020.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $a_1,\ldots,a_{40}$ be real numbers with $\sum_{i=1}^{40}a_i=0$ and $|a_i-a_{i+1}|\le1$ for $1\le i\le40$, where $a_{41}=a_1$. Find the maximum possible values of (a) $a_{10}+a_{20}+a_{30}+a_{40}$ and (b) $a_{10}a_{20}+a_{30}a_{40}$.

cn.2022.1.3.text: Domain variant: AoPS asks for positive integers a; the inspected Chinese compilation asks for all integers a. The bank retains the positive-integer AoPS version. The condition depends only on a modulo 37.
cn.2022.1.3.reviewed_statement: Find all positive integers $a$ for which there exists a set $X$ of six integers such that for every $k=1,2,\ldots,36$ there are $x,y\in X$ with $$ax+y\equiv k\pmod{37}.$$

cn.2023.1.3.text: The Chinese compilation mislabels the white matching using m instead of n. The white matching has n pairs, as required by its 2n white vertices and confirmed by the AoPS paper.
cn.2023.1.3.reviewed_statement: Color the vertices of a regular $(2m+2n)$-gon, where $m,n$ are positive integers, with $2m$ black and $2n$ white vertices. The coloring distance between two vertices of the same color is the smaller number of opposite-colored vertices on the two boundary paths joining them. A black matching pairs all black vertices with $m$ pairwise nonintersecting segments; define $P(B)$ as the sum of the coloring distances of its pairs. Define a white matching and $P(W)$ analogously using all $2n$ white vertices. Prove that $$\max_B P(B)=\max_W P(W)$$ for every coloring.

cn.2024.1.1.text: The AoPS public transcription mistakenly lists x_1,...,x_n before a product of 2023 factors. The inspected Chinese paper confirms exactly 2023 positive integer factors.
cn.2024.1.1.reviewed_statement: Find the smallest real $\lambda$ such that every positive integer $n$ can be written as $n=x_1x_2\cdots x_{2023}$ with positive integers $x_i$, each of which is either prime or at most $n^\lambda$.

cn.2024.2.4.text: The bank retains the exact maximum-cardinality question in the inspected Chinese paper; the AoPS reproduction additionally requests equality cases for its stated bound.
cn.2024.2.4.reviewed_statement: Nonnegative real numbers $a_1,\ldots,a_{2023}$ have sum $100$. Let $$A=\{(i,j):1\le i\le j\le2023,\ a_ia_j\ge1\}.$$ Find the maximum possible value of $|A|$.

cn.2025.1.1.text: The public AoPS transcription omits that x_1 is a positive integer. This condition is explicit in the inspected Chinese paper reproduction and is restored.
cn.2025.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $\alpha>1$ be irrational and let $L$ be a positive integer with $L>\alpha^2/(\alpha-1)$. Starting from a positive integer $x_1>L$, define $$x_{n+1}=\begin{cases}\lfloor\alpha x_n\rfloor,&x_n\le L,\\\lfloor x_n/\alpha\rfloor,&x_n>L.\end{cases}$$ Prove that the sequence is eventually periodic and that its eventual least positive period is odd and independent of $x_1$.

cn.2025.2.6.text: The inspected SM International Education paper reproduction confirms n>=4 and the n^(-3/2) improvement, matching AoPS. A separate Beijing information-site transcription has a garbled formula and n>=3 and was not used for this problem.
cn.2025.2.6.reviewed_statement: Real numbers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ satisfy $$\sum_{i=1}^n a_i=n,\qquad\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2=2n,\qquad\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^3=3n.$$ (a) Find the largest constant $C$ such that $$\max_i a_i-\min_i a_i\ge C$$ for all $n\ge4$. (b) Prove that there is a constant $C_2>0$, independent of $n$ and the numbers, such that $$\max_i a_i-\min_i a_i\ge C+C_2 n^{-3/2}.$$

cz.1963.0.4.reviewed_statement: Two quadratic equations $$x^2+ax+b=0,\qquad x^2+cx+d=0$$ with real coefficients are given. Find necessary and sufficient conditions for the first equation to have real roots $x,x_1$ and the second real roots $x,x_2$ with $x>0$ and $x_1>x_2$.

cz.1964.0.2.reviewed_statement: $PP'$ and $QQ'$ are skew rays, and points $X$ and $Y$ start simultaneously from $P$ and $Q$ and move along the rays $PP'$ and $QQ'$ with constant speeds $c_1$ and $c_2$. Prove that the midpoint $Z$ of $XY$ always lies on a fixed ray $RR'$, where $R$ is the midpoint of $PQ$.

cz.1965.0.1.reviewed_statement: Prove that $5^{2n+1}2^{n+2}+3^{n+2}2^{2n+1}$ is divisible by $19$ for every non-negative integer $n$.

Discuss the conditions of solvability in terms of $d$ and $v$.

cz.1965.0.3.reviewed_statement: Solve in the real numbers the equation $$\sqrt{x^2-2x-1}+\sqrt{x^2+2x-1}=p,$$ where $p$ is a given real number. Discuss the solvability with respect to the number $p$.

cz.1965.0.4.reviewed_statement:
A vessel has the shape of a hollow cube placed so that its space diagonal $AP$ is in a vertical position, and $AP=1$. There is water in the vessel; the part of the space diagonal $AP$ that is submerged in the water has length $x$.

Express the volume $y$ of the water in the vessel in terms of the number $x$ for these two cases:

a) $0<x\le\frac{1}{3}$;

b) $\frac{1}{3}<x\le\frac{1}{2}$.

cz.1966.0.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1966.0.1.reviewed_statement: Consider the system of inequalities $$y-x\geq|x+1|-|x-1|,\qquad |y-x|-y+x\geq 2.$$ Draw the solution sets of the two inequalities in the plane and highlight the solution set of the system.

cz.1966.0.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1966.0.2.reviewed_statement: In the plane, $n$ circles are given, any two of which intersect in exactly two points, and no point of the plane lies on three of these circles. Determine the total number of parts into which the system of circles divides the plane. (For example, three circles with these properties divide the plane into eight parts.)

cz.1966.0.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1966.0.3.reviewed_statement:
A square $ABCD$ with centre $S$ and side $s=AB=1$ is given. Further, two points $E$, $F$ are given, lying respectively on the lines $BC$, $AD$ in the interior of the half-plane opposite to $CDA$.

On the basis of a computation, determine all triangles $XYZ$ whose vertices $X$, $Y$, $Z$ lie respectively on the segments $CD$, $AD$, $BC$ and whose lines $XY$, $YZ$, $ZX$ pass respectively through the points $E$, $S$, $F$. (Remark. By computation determine, for example, the length $CX$.)

cz.1966.0.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1966.0.4.reviewed_statement:
Two triangles $ABC$ and $ABD$ with a common side of length $c$ are placed in space. The triangle $ABC$ is right-angled with hypotenuse $AB$, the triangle $ABD$ is equilateral, and the planes $ABC$, $ABD$ make the angle $\varphi$.

a) Express the distance of the points $C$, $D$ in terms of the side lengths of both triangles and the number $\varphi$; determine this distance by a construction.

b) Find an angle $\varphi$ such that the tetrahedron $ABCD$ has four congruent edges.

cz.1969.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.

Prove that the area $P$ of every convex quadrilateral whose vertices are the points $A,B,C,D$ always satisfies $$P\leq\frac{1}{2}(OA+OD)(OB+OC),$$ and find when equality holds.

cz.1969.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1969.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $p$ be a prime. How many different sequences of positive integers $$a_0,a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n,\ldots$$ are there such that for every positive integer $n=1,2,3,\ldots$ $$\frac{a_0}{a_1}+\frac{a_0}{a_2}+\cdots+\frac{a_0}{a_n}+\frac{p}{a_{n+1}}=1?$$

cz.1969.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1969.2.4.reviewed_statement: Find all complex numbers $z$ such that $$\Bigl|z-\bigl|z+|z|\bigr|\Bigr|-|z|\sqrt{3}\geq 0,$$ and draw this set in the complex plane.

cz.1969.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1969.2.5.reviewed_statement: Two perpendicular lines $p,q$ and a point $A\notin p\cup q$ are given in the plane. Find the locus of the points $X$ such that $$XA=\sqrt{d(X,p)\cdot d(X,q)},$$ where $d(X,p)$ denotes the distance from $X$ to $p$.

cz.1969.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1969.2.6.reviewed_statement:
Circles $k_0,k_1,\ldots,k_n$ $(n\geq 3)$ of equal radius $r$ lie on a sphere of radius $1$. The circle $k_0$ is tangent to all the other circles, and $k_i$ is tangent to $k_{i+1}$ for $i=1,\ldots,n$ (with $k_{n+1}=k_1$). (Two circles on the sphere are tangent if they have exactly one common point and the same tangent line there.)

(a) Find the relation between $n$ and $r$.

(b) For which $n$ is such a configuration possible, and what is the corresponding radius $r$?

cz.1971.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,c$ be real numbers. Prove that there exist non-negative numbers $x,y,z$, not all equal to zero, which satisfy the inequalities $$cy-bz\geq 0,\qquad az-cx\geq 0,\qquad bx-ay\geq 0.$$

cz.1971.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1971.1.2.reviewed_statement: For a triangle $ABC$, points $D\neq B$ and $E\neq A$ are constructed on the line $AB$ such that $DA=BE=AB$. Find a necessary and sufficient condition on the lengths of the segments $a=BC$, $b=AC$ for a triangle $ABC$ to exist in which the angle $DCE$ is right.

cz.1971.1.3.reviewed_statement: The positive integers $2,3,4,5,\ldots,n-1,n$ are given, where $n\geq 96$. Prove that if they are divided arbitrarily into two groups, then in at least one of the groups one can always find two (distinct) numbers together with their product.\n\nFind an example showing that the statement does not hold for $n=95$.

cz.1971.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1971.2.4.reviewed_statement: Prove that there are real numbers $A,B$ such that $$\sum_{k=1}^n\tan k\,\tan(k-1)=A\tan n+Bn$$ for every positive integer $n$.

Choose a point $X$ of the segment $AB$ and a point $Y\neq X$ of the ray $AC$, and construct in the plane $ABC$ an equilateral triangle $XYZ$. Investigate the set $M$ of the vertices $Z$ of all equilateral triangles $XYZ$ constructed in this way, as the point $X$ runs over the segment $AB$ and the point $Y$ over the ray $AC$. Investigate also the case $\angle BAC=60^\circ$.

cz.1971.2.6.reviewed_statement: A tetrahedron $ABCD$ and an interior point $O$ are given. For each edge $e$ of the tetrahedron let $f(e)$ be the segment through $O$ parallel to $e$ with endpoints on the faces of the tetrahedron. Prove that $$\sum_e\frac{f(e)}{e}=3,$$ where the sum is over the six edges.

cz.1972.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1972.1.3.reviewed_statement:
The polynomials $P_n$ are defined by $P_0(x)=2$, $P_1(x)=x$ and $P_{n+1}(x)+P_{n-1}(x)=xP_n(x)$ for $n\geq 1$.

(a) Find the polynomial $$Q_n(x)=P_n^2(x)-xP_n(x)P_{n-1}(x)+P_{n-1}^2(x)$$ for $n=1972$.

(b) Express $\big(P_{n+1}(x)-P_{n-1}(x)\big)^2$ in terms of $P_n(x)$ and $Q_n(x)$.

cz.1972.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1972.2.4.reviewed_statement: Prove that there are infinitely many positive integers $a$ such that $n^4+a$ is composite for every positive integer $n$. Give five such numbers $a$.

cz.1972.2.5.reviewed_statement: How many pairs of mutually disjoint subsets does a set with $n$ elements have?

cz.1972.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1972.2.6.reviewed_statement: Two distinct points $A,S$ are given in a plane $\varrho$. Further, positive numbers $d,\omega$ with $\omega<180$ are given. Construct all points $X$ of the plane $\varrho$ with the following property: the rotation in the plane $\varrho$ about the centre $S$ in the positive sense through the angle $\omega^\circ$ takes the point $X$ to a point $X'$ such that $XX'=d$ and the point $A$ lies on the segment $XX'$. What condition must the numbers $d,\omega$ satisfy for such a point $X$ to exist?

cz.1973.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1973.1.1.reviewed_statement: The angles of a triangle satisfy $$\sin^2\alpha+\sin^2\beta+\sin^2\gamma=2.$$ Prove that the triangle is right-angled.

cz.1973.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1973.1.2.reviewed_statement: A tetrahedron is given. Let $v_i$ $(i=1,2,3,4)$ denote its altitudes and $\varrho_i$ $(i=1,2,3,4)$ the radii of the spheres escribed to this tetrahedron. Prove that $$2\left(\frac{1}{v_1}+\frac{1}{v_2}+\frac{1}{v_3}+\frac{1}{v_4}\right)=\frac{1}{\varrho_1}+\frac{1}{\varrho_2}+\frac{1}{\varrho_3}+\frac{1}{\varrho_4}.$$

cz.1973.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.

cz.1973.2.5.reviewed_statement:
A plane $\varrho$ is given. For two points $P,Q$ of $\varrho$ let $P+Q$ denote the midpoint of the pair $P,Q$, and $P\cdot Q$ the point of the plane $\varrho$ obtained by rotating the point $Q$ about the point $P$ through $90^\circ$ in the positive sense.

a) Are these operations commutative?

b) Two fixed distinct points $A,B$ of the plane $\varrho$ are given. The equation $$Y\cdot X=(A\cdot X)+B$$ determines a map $X\mapsto Y$. Determine what kind of map it is.

c) Construct all fixed points of this map.

cz.1974.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.

Prove that there is a positive number $k$ such that $|a|\leq k$ for all $f\in\mathcal{M}$, and find the least such $k$.

Find the locus of the points $X$ for which the area of $\mathcal{D}\cup\mathcal{D}_X$ is at most $1.5$.

(1) there is $(a,b)\in\mathbf{M}$ with $ab(a-b)\neq 0$;

(2) if $(x_1,y_1),(x_2,y_2)\in\mathbf{M}$ and $c\in\mathbb{R}$, then $(cx_1,cy_1)$, $(x_1+x_2,y_1+y_2)$ and $(x_1x_2,y_1y_2)$ belong to $\mathbf{M}$.
