cz.1988.2.4.reviewed_statement: Prove that the numbers $1,2,3,\ldots,2^n$ can be coloured red and blue so that no non-constant arithmetic progression of $2n$ terms chosen from them is monochromatic.

cz.1988.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1988.2.5.reviewed_statement: Find all $a\in(-2,2)$ for which the polynomial $x^{154}-ax^{77}+1$ is divisible by $x^{14}-ax^7+1$.

cz.1988.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1988.2.6.reviewed_statement: Three points are given inside a triangle $A_1A_2A_3$ with sides $a_1,a_2,a_3$; they are labelled $P_1,P_2,P_3$ so that the product of their distances from the corresponding sides $a_1,a_2,a_3$ is as large as possible. Prove that the triangles $P_1A_2A_3$, $A_1P_2A_3$, $A_1A_2P_3$ cover the triangle $A_1A_2A_3$.

cz.1989.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1989.1.1.reviewed_statement: Three distinct points $A,B,C$ on a circle with centre $S$ and a line $p$ perpendicular to $AS$ are given. Let $D$ and $E$ be the intersections of $p$ with the lines $AB$ and $AC$. Prove that $B,C,D,E$ are concyclic.

cz.1989.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1989.1.2.reviewed_statement: $mn$ segments join pairs of $n$ given points in the plane. Prove that one can choose a sequence $V_0,V_1,\ldots,V_m$ of distinct points among them such that $V_{i-1}$ and $V_i$ are joined by a segment for $1\leq i\leq m$.

cz.1989.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1989.1.3.reviewed_statement: For given relatively prime numbers $p>q>0$, find all pairs of real numbers $c,d$ such that the sets $$A=\left\{\left\lfloor n\frac{p}{q}\right\rfloor:n\in\mathbb{N}\right\},\qquad B=\{\lfloor cn+d\rfloor:n\in\mathbb{N}\}$$ satisfy $A\cap B=\emptyset$ and $A\cup B=\mathbb{N}$.

cz.1989.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1989.2.4.reviewed_statement: The sides of a triangle $T'$ are equal to the medians of a triangle $T$. Prove that if $T$ and $T'$ have a common angle, they are similar.

cz.1989.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1989.2.5.reviewed_statement: Each cell of a $2\times n$ table is coloured black or white so that no $2\times 2$ square is completely black. Let $P_n$ be the number of such colourings. Prove that $P_{1989}$ is divisible by $3$ and find the highest power of $3$ dividing it.

cz.1989.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1989.2.6.reviewed_statement: A finite sequence $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ of positive integers not exceeding $n$ has any two neighbouring terms different, and no four terms satisfy $a_p=a_r\neq a_q=a_s$ for $p<q<r<s$. Find the maximum number of terms of such a sequence.

cz.1990.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1990.1.1.reviewed_statement: The sequence $(a_n)_{n\geq 1}$ is given by $a_1=1$ and $a_{2^k+j}=-a_j$ for all $k\geq 0$, $1\leq j\leq 2^k$. Prove that the sequence is not periodic.

cz.1990.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1990.1.2.reviewed_statement: Find all $\alpha\in\mathbb{R}$ with the following property: whenever positive numbers $x,y,z$ satisfy $$x^2+y^2+z^2\leq\alpha(xy+yz+zx),$$ they are the sides of a triangle.

cz.1990.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1990.1.3.reviewed_statement: $ABCDEFGH$ is a cube. Consider planes whose intersection with the tetrahedron $ABDE$ is a triangle with an obtuse angle $\varphi$. Find all $\varphi>\frac{\pi}{2}$ for which such a plane exists.

cz.1990.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1990.2.4.reviewed_statement: Find the largest $k\geq 0$ such that $$\left(\sum_{j=1}^nx_j\right)^2\left(\sum_{j=1}^nx_jx_{j+1}\right)\geq k\sum_{j=1}^nx_j^2x_{j+1}^2$$ for every $n\geq 2$ and all non-negative numbers $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ (where $x_{n+1}=x_1$).

cz.1990.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1990.2.5.reviewed_statement: In a country any two towns are joined by exactly one road. Each road is one-way and is intended either only for motor vehicles or only for cyclists. Roads cross only in towns (elsewhere they have grade-separated crossings). Prove that there is a town from which one can travel to any other town without changing the means of transport.

cz.1990.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1990.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $k\geq 1$ be an integer. Prove that there is a family $\mathsf{S}$ of two-element subsets of $\{1,\ldots,2k\}$ with the following property: whenever sets $\mathsf{M}_1,\ldots,\mathsf{M}_{2k}$ satisfy $\mathsf{M}_i\cap\mathsf{M}_j\neq\emptyset\iff\{i,j\}\in\mathsf{S}$, the union $\mathsf{M}_1\cup\cdots\cup\mathsf{M}_{2k}$ has at least $k^2$ elements.

cz.1991.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1991.1.1.reviewed_statement: Prove that for all real numbers $p,q,r,\varphi$ $$p\cos^2\varphi+q\sin\varphi\cos\varphi+r\sin^2\varphi\geq\frac{1}{2}\left(p+r-\sqrt{(p-r)^2+q^2}\right).$$

cz.1991.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1991.1.2.reviewed_statement: A museum has the shape of a (not necessarily convex) $3n$-gon. Prove that $n$ guards can be positioned so that they watch the whole museum.

cz.1991.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1991.1.3.reviewed_statement: For a permutation $p$ of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ let $d(p)=|p(1)-1|+|p(2)-2|+\cdots+|p(n)-n|$, and let $i(p)$ be the number of inversions of $p$ (pairs $i<j$ with $p(i)>p(j)$). Prove that $d(p)\leq 2i(p)$.

cz.1991.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1991.2.4.reviewed_statement: Prove that in every triangle $ABC$ with $\angle A=2\angle B$ the ratio of the distance from $C$ to $A$ to the distance from $C$ to the perpendicular bisector of $AB$ is the same.

cz.1991.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1991.2.5.reviewed_statement: In a group of mathematicians everybody has at least one friend (friendship is mutual). Prove that some mathematician's friends have on average at least as many friends as the average number of friends in the whole group.

cz.1991.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1991.2.6.reviewed_statement: The set $\mathbb{N}$ of all positive integers is the union of three subsets $A_1,A_2,A_3$. Prove that at least one of them has the following property: there is a positive number $m$ such that for every $k$ one can find in this subset numbers $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_k$ with $0<a_{j+1}-a_j\leq m$ for $1\leq j\leq k-1$.

cz.1992.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1992.1.1.reviewed_statement: For a permutation $(a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{17})$ of $1,2,\ldots,17$ let $k_p$ be the largest $k$ with $a_1+\cdots+a_k<a_{k+1}+\cdots+a_{17}$. Find the maximum and the minimum of $k_p$ and the sum $\sum_pk_p$ over all permutations $p$.

cz.1992.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1992.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $S$ be the total surface area of a tetrahedron with edges $a,b,c,d,e,f$. Prove that $$S\leq\frac{\sqrt{3}}{6}\left(a^2+b^2+\cdots+f^2\right).$$

cz.1992.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1992.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $S(n)$ be the sum of the digits of $n\in\mathbb{N}$. Find all $n$ such that $S(n)=S(2n)=S(3n)=\cdots=S(n^2)$.

cz.1992.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.

cz.1992.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1992.2.5.reviewed_statement: The function $f:(0,1)\to\mathbb{R}$ is defined by $f(x)=x$ if $x$ is irrational and $f(x)=\frac{p+1}{q}$ if $x=\frac{p}{q}$ with $\gcd(p,q)=1$. Find the maximum of $f$ on the interval $\left(\frac{7}{8},\frac{8}{9}\right)$.

cz.1992.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1992.2.6.reviewed_statement: $ABC$ is an acute triangle. The altitude from $B$ meets the circle with diameter $AC$ at $P,Q$, and the altitude from $C$ meets the circle with diameter $AB$ at $M,N$. Prove that $M,N,P,Q$ are concyclic.

cz.1993.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1993.1.1.reviewed_statement: Find all positive integers $n$ for which $7^n-1$ is divisible by $6^n-1$.

cz.1993.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1993.1.2.reviewed_statement: Integers are written in the cells of a $19\times 19$ table so that numbers in any two cells sharing a side differ by at most $2$. Find the greatest possible number of distinct integers in the table.

cz.1993.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1993.1.3.reviewed_statement: In the plane, a triangle $AKL$ with $\angle ALK>90^\circ+\angle LAK$ is given. Construct an isosceles trapezoid $ABCD$ with $AB\parallel CD$ such that the point $K$ lies on the side $BC$, the point $L$ lies on the diagonal $AC$, and the intersection $S$ of the segments $AK$ and $BL$ is the centre of the circle circumscribed to the trapezoid $ABCD$.

cz.1993.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1993.2.4.reviewed_statement: The sequence of positive integers $(a_n)$ is defined by $a_1=2$ and, for $n\geq 1$, $a_{n+1}$ is the sum of the tenth powers of the decimal digits of $a_n$. Does some number occur twice in the sequence?

cz.1993.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1993.2.5.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$ such that $f(-1)=f(1)$ and $$f(x)+f(y)=f(x+2xy)+f(y-2xy)$$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$.

cz.1993.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1993.2.6.reviewed_statement: Prove that there is a tetrahedron that can be partitioned into eight congruent tetrahedra, each similar to the original one.

cz.1994.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1994.1.1.reviewed_statement: A function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ satisfies $f(x)+f(x+2)\leq 2f(x+1)$ for all $x\in\mathbb{N}$. Prove that some line in the coordinate plane contains infinitely many points $(n,f(n))$, $n\in\mathbb{N}$.

cz.1994.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1994.1.2.reviewed_statement: A cuboid of volume $V$ contains a convex polyhedron $M$ whose orthogonal projection on each face of the cuboid covers the whole face. What is the least possible volume of $M$?

cz.1994.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.

cz.1994.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1994.2.4.reviewed_statement: A sequence of positive integers $a_1,a_2,\ldots$ is such that for every $n$ the product $(a_n-1)(a_n-2)\cdots(a_n-n^2)$ is a positive multiple of $n^{n^2-1}$. Prove that for every finite set $P$ of primes $$\sum_{p\in P}\frac{1}{\log_pa_p}<1.$$

cz.1994.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1994.2.5.reviewed_statement: In an acute triangle $ABC$ the altitudes $AA_1$, $BB_1$, $CC_1$ meet at $V$. If the triangles $AC_1V$, $BA_1V$, $CB_1V$ have equal areas, must the triangle $ABC$ be equilateral?

cz.1994.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1994.2.6.reviewed_statement: Prove that among any four distinct numbers in the interval $(0,1)$ one can choose two, $a$ and $b$, such that $$\sqrt{(1-a^2)(1-b^2)}>\frac{a}{2b}+\frac{b}{2a}-ab-\frac{1}{8ab}.$$

cz.1995.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1995.1.1.reviewed_statement: A tetrahedron $ABCD$ satisfies $\angle BAC+\angle CAD+\angle DAB=\angle ABC+\angle CBD+\angle DBA=180^\circ$. Prove that $CD\geq AB$.

cz.1995.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1995.1.2.reviewed_statement: Find the positive real numbers $x,y$ for which $$\frac{x+y}{2},\quad\sqrt{xy},\quad\frac{2xy}{x+y},\quad\sqrt{\frac{x^2+y^2}{2}}$$ are integers with sum $66$.

cz.1995.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1995.1.3.reviewed_statement: Five distinct points and five distinct lines are given in the plane. Prove that one can choose two of the points and two of the lines so that neither chosen line contains a chosen point.

cz.1995.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1995.2.4.reviewed_statement: Are there $10000$ ten-digit numbers divisible by $7$, any two of which can be obtained from each other by permuting the digits?

cz.1995.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1995.2.5.reviewed_statement: Points $A$ and $B$ are given on a circle $k$ with centre $S$ so that the chord $AB$ is seen from $S$ at an angle of $90^\circ$. Circles $k_1$, $k_2$ touch the circle $k$ internally at the points $A$, $B$ respectively, and moreover touch each other externally at a point $Z$. A circle $k_3$ lying inside the angle $ASB$ touches the circle $k$ (internally) at a point $C$ and touches the circles $k_1$, $k_2$ (externally) at points $X$, $Y$ respectively. Prove that the segment $XY$ is seen from the point $C$ at an angle of $45^\circ$.

cz.1995.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1995.2.6.reviewed_statement: Find all real parameters $p$ for which the equation $$x^3-2p(p+1)x^2+(p^4+4p^3-1)x-3p^3=0$$ has three distinct real roots that are the sides of a right triangle.

cz.1996.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.

cz.1996.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1996.1.2.reviewed_statement: $AP$, $BQ$, $CR$ are the altitudes of an acute triangle $ABC$. Prove that for every point $X$ inside the triangle $PQR$ there is a tetrahedron $ABCD$ such that $X$ is the point of the face $ABC$ farthest from $D$, distances being measured along the surface of the tetrahedron.

cz.1996.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1996.1.3.reviewed_statement: Six three-element subsets of a finite set $X$ are given. Prove that the elements of $X$ can be coloured in two colours so that none of the given subsets is monochromatic.

cz.1996.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1996.2.4.reviewed_statement: Points $A$ and $B$ on the rays $CX$ and $CY$ of an acute angle $XCY$ satisfy $CX<CA=CB<CY$. Construct a line meeting the ray $CX$ and the segments $AB$, $BC$ at $K$, $L$, $M$ respectively such that $$KA\cdot YB=XA\cdot MB=LA\cdot LB\neq 0.$$

cz.1996.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1996.2.5.reviewed_statement: For which integers $k$ is there a function $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ such that $f(1995)=1996$ and $$f(xy)=f(x)+f(y)+kf(\gcd(x,y))$$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{N}$?

cz.1996.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1996.2.6.reviewed_statement: Points $K,L,M$ on the sides $AB$, $BC$, $CA$ of a triangle $ABC$ satisfy $\frac{AK}{AB}=\frac{BL}{BC}=\frac{CM}{CA}=\frac{1}{3}$. Prove that if the circumcircles of the triangles $AKM$, $BLK$, $CML$ are congruent, then so are their incircles.

cz.1997.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1997.1.1.reviewed_statement: A triangle $ABC$ has sides $a,b,c$ and opposite angles $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$. Prove that if $\alpha=3\beta$, then $(a^2-b^2)(a-b)=bc^2$. Is the converse true?

cz.1997.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1997.1.2.reviewed_statement: Each side and diagonal of a regular $n$-gon ($n\geq 3$ odd) is coloured red or blue. In one move one may choose a vertex and change the colours of all segments issuing from it. Prove that, whatever the initial colouring, one can achieve that the number of blue segments at each vertex is even, and that the resulting colouring depends only on the initial colouring.

cz.1997.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1997.1.3.reviewed_statement: A tetrahedron $ABCD$ is divided without remainder into five convex polyhedra in such a way that none of its faces is divided and the intersection of any two of the five resulting polyhedra is either a common vertex, or a common edge, or a common face. What is the least possible sum of the numbers of faces of these five polyhedra?

cz.1997.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1997.2.4.reviewed_statement:
Prove that there exists an increasing sequence $(a_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of positive integers such that for every positive integer $k\geq 2$ the sequence $(k+a_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ contains only finitely many primes.

Decide whether there exists an increasing sequence $(a_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of positive integers such that for every integer $k\geq 0$ the sequence $(k+a_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ contains only finitely many primes.

cz.1997.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1997.2.5.reviewed_statement: For a given integer $n\geq 2$ find the maximum of $$V_n=\sin x_1\cos x_2+\sin x_2\cos x_3+\cdots+\sin x_n\cos x_1$$ over real numbers $x_1,\ldots,x_n$.

cz.1997.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1997.2.6.reviewed_statement: A parallelogram $ABCD$ is given such that $ABD$ is an acute triangle and $\angle BAD=45^\circ$. In the interiors of the sides of the parallelogram one can choose, in various ways, points $K\in AB$, $L\in BC$, $M\in CD$ and $N\in DA$ so that $KLMN$ is a cyclic quadrilateral whose circumcircle has the same radius as both circumcircles of the triangles $ANK$ and $CLM$. Find the set of intersection points of the diagonals of all such quadrilaterals $KLMN$.

cz.1998.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1998.1.1.reviewed_statement: Solve the equation $$x\cdot\lfloor x\cdot\lfloor x\cdot\lfloor x\rfloor\rfloor\rfloor=88$$ in the set of positive real numbers, where $\lfloor a\rfloor$ denotes the integer part of a real number $a$, i.e. the integer for which $\lfloor a\rfloor\leq a<\lfloor a\rfloor+1$. For example, $\lfloor 3.7\rfloor=3$ and $\lfloor 6\rfloor=6$.

cz.1998.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1998.1.2.reviewed_statement: Prove that for any set of $14$ distinct positive integers there are $k$ $(1\leq k\leq 7)$ and two disjoint $k$-element subsets $\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}$ and $\{b_1,\ldots,b_k\}$ such that $A=\frac{1}{a_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{a_k}$ and $B=\frac{1}{b_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{b_k}$ satisfy $|A-B|<0.001$.

cz.1998.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1998.1.3.reviewed_statement: A sphere is inscribed in a tetrahedron $ABCD$. The tangent planes to the sphere parallel to the faces of the tetrahedron cut off four smaller tetrahedra. Prove that the sum of the $24$ edges of the smaller tetrahedra equals twice the sum of the edges of $ABCD$.

cz.1998.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1998.2.4.reviewed_statement: For each date of the year $1998$ the number $\text{day}^{\text{month}}-\text{year}$ is computed, together with the highest power of $3$ dividing it; e.g. for April $21$ we get $21^4-1998=192483=3^3\cdot 7129$, divisible by $3^3$ but not by $3^4$. Find all dates for which this power of $3$ is the highest.

cz.1998.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1998.2.5.reviewed_statement: A circle $k$ and a point $A$ outside it are given in the plane. Prove that all trapezoids inscribed in $k$ whose legs (extended) meet at $A$ have the same intersection point of the diagonals.

cz.1998.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1998.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,c$ be positive numbers. Prove that there is a triangle with sides $a,b,c$ if and only if the system $$\frac{y}{z}+\frac{z}{y}=\frac{a}{x},\qquad\frac{z}{x}+\frac{x}{z}=\frac{b}{y},\qquad\frac{x}{y}+\frac{y}{x}=\frac{c}{z}$$ has a real solution.

cz.1999.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1999.1.1.reviewed_statement:
Into the numerator and the denominator of the fraction $$\frac{29:28:27:26:25:24:23:22:21:20:19:18:17:16}{15:14:13:12:11:10:9:8:7:6:5:4:3:2}$$ we may repeatedly insert brackets, always at the same places one below the other.

a) Find the smallest possible integer value of the resulting expression.

b) Find all possible integer values of the resulting expression.

cz.1999.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1999.1.2.reviewed_statement: In a tetrahedron $ABCD$, $E$ and $F$ are the midpoints of the medians from $A$ and $D$ (a median joins a vertex to the centroid of the opposite face). Find the ratio of the volumes of the tetrahedra $BCEF$ and $ABCD$.

cz.1999.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1999.1.3.reviewed_statement: Prove that there is a triangle $ABC$ with $a\neq b$ and $a+t_a=b+t_b$, where $t_a,t_b$ are the medians to the sides $a,b$. Prove also that there is a number $k$ such that every such triangle satisfies $a+t_a=b+t_b=k(a+b)$, and find all possible ratios $a:b$ in such triangles.

cz.1999.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1999.2.4.reviewed_statement:
A language has only two letters, $A$ and $B$, and:

(i) there are no words of length $1$, and the only words of length $2$ are $AB$ and $BB$;

(ii) a string of length $n>2$ is a word if and only if it can be obtained from a word of length less than $n$ by replacing each letter $B$ by some (not necessarily the same) word.

Prove that the number of words of length $n$ equals $\frac{2^n+2\cdot(-1)^n}{3}$.

cz.1999.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1999.2.5.reviewed_statement: Given an acute angle $APX$ in the plane, construct a square $ABCD$ such that $P$ lies on the side $BC$ and the ray $PX$ meets $CD$ at a point $Q$ with $AP$ bisecting the angle $BAQ$.

cz.1999.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the Czechoslovak MO annual report (final round, category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.1999.2.6.reviewed_statement: Find all pairs of real numbers $a,b$ for which the system $$\frac{x+y}{x^2+y^2}=a,\qquad\frac{x^3+y^3}{x^2+y^2}=b$$ has a real solution.

cz.2000.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2000.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Prove that the sum $4\cdot 3^{2^n}+3\cdot 4^{2^n}$ is divisible by $13$ if and only if $n$ is even.

cz.2000.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2000.1.2.reviewed_statement: An isosceles triangle $ABC$ with base $AB$ is given. A point $P$ is chosen on its altitude $CD$ so that the incircles of the triangle $ABP$ and of the quadrilateral $PECF$ are congruent; here $E$ is the intersection of the line $AP$ with the side $BC$ and $F$ is the intersection of the line $BP$ with the side $AC$. Prove that the incircles of the triangles $ADP$ and $BCP$ are also congruent.

cz.2000.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2000.1.3.reviewed_statement: In the plane, $2000$ congruent triangles of area $1$ are given, which are images of one and the same triangle under different translations. Each of these triangles contains the centroids of all the others. Prove that the area of the union of these triangles is less than $\frac{22}{9}$.

cz.2000.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2000.2.4.reviewed_statement: For which quadratic functions $f(x)$ does there exist a quadratic function $g(x)$ such that the roots of the equation $g\bigl(f(x)\bigr)=0$ are four distinct consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression and at the same time they are also roots of the equation $f(x)g(x)=0$?

cz.2000.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2000.2.5.reviewed_statement: Monika made a paper model of a triangular pyramid whose base was a right triangle. When she cut the model along the legs of the base and along a median of one of the faces, after unfolding it into the plane she obtained a square with side $a$. Determine the volume of this pyramid.

cz.2000.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2000.2.6.reviewed_statement: Find all four-digit numbers $\overline{abcd}$ (in the decimal system) for which the equality $$\overline{abcd}+1=(\overline{ac}+1)(\overline{bd}+1)$$ holds.

cz.2001.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2001.1.1.reviewed_statement: Determine all polynomials $P(x)$ with real coefficients such that for all real numbers $x$ $$\bigl(P(x)\bigr)^2+P(-x)=P(x^2)+P(x).$$

cz.2001.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2001.1.2.reviewed_statement: In the plane, a triangle $PQX$ is given with $|PQ|=3\text{ cm}$, $|PX|=2.6\text{ cm}$, $|QX|=3.8\text{ cm}$. Construct a right triangle $ABC$ such that its incircle touches the hypotenuse $AB$ at the point $P$ and the leg $BC$ at the point $Q$, and such that the point $X$ lies on the line $AC$.

cz.2001.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2001.1.3.reviewed_statement: Find all triples of real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ for which the set of all solutions of the inequality $$\sqrt{2x^2+ax+b}>x-c$$ with unknown $x$ is the set $(-\infty,0]\cup(1,\infty)$.

cz.2001.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2001.2.4.reviewed_statement: A certain language has $n$ letters. A group of letters (written one after another) is a word if and only if there are no two equal letters between any two equal letters. Determine the number of all words of maximal length.

cz.2001.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2001.2.5.reviewed_statement: An isosceles trapezoid $C_1AB_2C_2$ with the shorter base $B_2C_2$ was cut out of paper. Let $B_1$ be the foot of the perpendicular from the midpoint $D$ of the leg $C_1C_2$ to the base $AC_1$. After folding the paper along the segments $DB_1$, $AD$ and $AC_2$, the points $C_1$, $C_2$ moved in space into one point $C$ and the points $B_1$, $B_2$ into the point $B$. This produced a model of a tetrahedron $ABCD$ with volume $64\text{ cm}^3$. Determine the side lengths of the original trapezoid.

cz.2001.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2001.2.6.reviewed_statement: Positive integers $a_1,a_2,\dots,a_n$ are given, together with a function $f\colon\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $f(x)=1$ for every integer $x<0$ and $$f(x)=1-f(x-a_1)\,f(x-a_2)\cdots f(x-a_n)$$ for every integer $x\ge 0$. Prove that there exist positive integers $s$ and $t$ such that $f(x+t)=f(x)$ for every integer $x>s$.

cz.2002.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2002.1.1.reviewed_statement: Solve in the set of integers the system of equations $$\begin{aligned}(4x)_5+7y&=14,\\(2y)_5-(3x)_7&=74,\end{aligned}$$ where $(n)_k$ denotes the multiple of the number $k$ closest to the number $n$.

cz.2002.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2002.1.2.reviewed_statement: Consider an arbitrary equilateral triangle $KLM$ whose vertices $K$, $L$ and $M$ lie on the sides $AB$, $BC$ and $CD$, respectively, of a given square $ABCD$. Find the set of midpoints of the sides of all such triangles $KLM$.

cz.2002.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2002.1.3.reviewed_statement: Prove that a positive integer $A$ is the square of a positive integer if and only if for every positive integer $n$ at least one of the differences $$(A+1)^2-A,\ (A+2)^2-A,\ (A+3)^2-A,\ \dots,\ (A+n)^2-A$$ is divisible by $n$.

cz.2002.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2002.2.4.reviewed_statement: Find all pairs of real numbers $a$, $b$ for which the equation $$\frac{ax^2-24x+b}{x^2-1}=x$$ has exactly two solutions in the set of real numbers, and the sum of these solutions is $12$.

cz.2002.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2002.2.5.reviewed_statement: In the plane, a triangle $KLM$ is given, together with a point $A$ lying on the ray opposite to the ray $KL$. Construct a rectangle $ABCD$ whose vertices $B$, $C$ and $D$ lie on the lines $KM$, $KL$ and $LM$, respectively.

cz.2002.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2002.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $\mathbb{R}^+$ be the set of all positive real numbers. Find all functions $f\colon\mathbb{R}^+\to\mathbb{R}^+$ satisfying, for arbitrary $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^+$, the equality $$f\bigl(xf(y)\bigr)=f(xy)+x.$$

cz.2003.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2003.1.1.reviewed_statement: Solve in the set of real numbers the system of equations $$\begin{aligned}x^2-xy+y^2&=7,\\x^2y+xy^2&=-2.\end{aligned}$$

cz.2003.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2003.1.2.reviewed_statement: Points $D$, $E$, $F$ are chosen in the interiors of the sides $BC$, $CA$, $AB$, respectively, of a given triangle $ABC$ so that the segments $AD$, $BE$, $CF$ intersect at one point, which we denote by $G$. Prove that if circles can be inscribed in the quadrilaterals $AFGE$, $BDGF$, $CEGD$ such that each two of them are externally tangent, then the triangle $ABC$ is equilateral.

cz.2003.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2003.1.3.reviewed_statement: A sequence $(x_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ with the first term $x_1=1$ satisfies, for every $n>1$, the condition $$x_n=\pm(n-1)x_{n-1}\pm(n-2)x_{n-2}\pm\dots\pm 2x_2\pm x_1$$ for a suitable choice of the signs “$+$” and “$-$”. Decide whether it is possible that the inequality $x_n\ne 12$ holds for only finitely many indices $n$.

cz.2003.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2003.2.4.reviewed_statement: An obtuse angle $AKS$ is given in the plane. Construct a triangle $ABC$ such that its side $BC$ lies on the line $KS$, the point $S$ is the midpoint of $BC$, and the point $K$ is the intersection of $BC$ with the bisector of the opposite angle $BAC$.

cz.2003.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2003.2.5.reviewed_statement: Show that in the numeral system with an arbitrary base $z\ge 3$ there exist two-digit numbers $A$ and $B$ which differ only in the order of their digits and have the following property: the quadratic equation $x^2-Ax+B=0$ has a double root in the set of real numbers. Prove also that for a given base $z$ such a pair $A$, $B$ is unique. For example, in the decimal system ($z=10$) these are only the numbers $A=18$ and $B=81$.

cz.2003.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2003.2.6.reviewed_statement: Prove that if the product of positive numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ equals $1$, then $$\frac{a}{b}+\frac{b}{c}+\frac{c}{a}\ge a+b+c.$$

cz.2004.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2004.1.1.reviewed_statement: Determine all triples $(x,y,z)$ of real numbers for which $$x^2+y^2+z^2\le 6+\min\left\{x^2-\frac{8}{x^4},\ y^2-\frac{8}{y^4},\ z^2-\frac{8}{z^4}\right\}.$$

cz.2004.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2004.1.2.reviewed_statement: For an arbitrary positive integer $n$, form from the letters $A$ and $B$ all possible “words” of length $n$, and let $p_n$ denote the number of those which contain neither four consecutive letters $AAAA$ nor three consecutive letters $BBB$. Determine the value of the expression $$\frac{p_{2004}-p_{2002}-p_{1999}}{p_{2001}+p_{2000}}.$$

cz.2004.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2004.1.3.reviewed_statement: In the plane, a circle $k$ and $121$ of its secants $p_1,p_2,\dots,p_{121}$ are given. On each line $p_i$ a point $A_i$ lying inside the circle is given. Prove that there exists a point $X$ on the circle $k$ such that the segment $A_iX$ forms an angle less than $21^\circ$ with the line $p_i$ for at least $29$ different indices $i$.

cz.2004.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2004.2.4.reviewed_statement: Determine for which positive integers $n$ the sum $$\frac{n}{1!}+\frac{n}{2!}+\dots+\frac{n}{n!}$$ is an integer.

cz.2004.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2004.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $L$ be an arbitrary interior point of the shorter arc $CD$ of the circumcircle of a square $ABCD$. Let $K$ be the intersection of the lines $AL$ and $CD$, $M$ the intersection of the lines $AD$ and $CL$, and $N$ the intersection of the lines $MK$ and $BC$. Prove that the points $B$, $L$, $M$, $N$ lie on one circle.

cz.2004.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2004.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $\mathbb{R}^+$ be the set of all positive real numbers. Determine all functions $f\colon\mathbb{R}^+\to\mathbb{R}^+$ which satisfy, for all positive numbers $x$, $y$, the equality $$x^2\bigl(f(x)+f(y)\bigr)=(x+y)\,f\bigl(f(x)y\bigr).$$

cz.2005.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2005.1.1.reviewed_statement: Consider arbitrary arithmetic progressions of real numbers $(x_i)_{i=1}^{\infty}$ and $(y_i)_{i=1}^{\infty}$ which have the same first term and satisfy, for some $k>1$, the equalities $$x_{k-1}y_{k-1}=42,\qquad x_ky_k=30\qquad\text{and}\qquad x_{k+1}y_{k+1}=16.$$ Find all such progressions for which the index $k$ is the largest possible.

cz.2005.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2005.1.2.reviewed_statement: Determine for which $m$ there exist exactly $2^{15}$ subsets $X$ of the set $\{1,2,3,\dots,47\}$ with the following property: the number $m$ is the smallest element of the set $X$, and for every $x\in X$ either $x+m\in X$ or $x+m>47$.

cz.2005.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2005.1.3.reviewed_statement: In a trapezoid $ABCD$ ($AB\parallel CD$), let $E$ be the midpoint of the leg $BC$. Prove that if both quadrilaterals $ABED$ and $AECD$ are tangential, then the side lengths of the trapezoid $ABCD$, denoted in the usual way, satisfy the equalities $$a+c=\frac{b}{3}+d\qquad\text{and}\qquad\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{c}=\frac{3}{b}.$$

cz.2005.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2005.2.4.reviewed_statement: An acute triangle $AKL$ is given in the plane. Consider an arbitrary rectangle $ABCD$ circumscribed about the triangle $AKL$ so that the point $K$ lies on the side $BC$ and the point $L$ lies on the side $CD$. Determine the locus of the intersections $S$ of the diagonals $AC$, $BD$ of all such rectangles $ABCD$.

cz.2005.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2005.2.5.reviewed_statement: Prove that for arbitrary real numbers $p$, $q$, $r$, $s$ with $q\ne -1$ and $s\ne -1$ the following holds: the quadratic equations $$x^2+px+q=0,\qquad x^2+rx+s=0$$ have a common root in the set of real numbers and their other roots are reciprocals of each other if and only if the coefficients $p$, $q$, $r$, $s$ satisfy the equalities $$pr=(q+1)(s+1)\qquad\text{and}\qquad p(q+1)s=r(s+1)q.$$ (A double root of a quadratic equation is counted twice.)

cz.2005.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2005.2.6.reviewed_statement: Decide whether for every ordering of the numbers $1,2,3,\dots,15$ these numbers can be written in at most four different colours so that all numbers of the same colour form, in the given order, a monotonic (i.e. increasing or decreasing) sequence. (A one-term sequence is monotonic.)

cz.2006.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2006.1.1.reviewed_statement: A sequence $(a_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ of positive integers has the property that for every $n\ge 1$ we have $a_{n+1}=a_n+b_n$, where $b_n$ is the number whose digits are those of $a_n$ in reverse order (unlike the notation of $a_n$, the notation of $b_n$ may begin with one or more zeros). For example, for $a_1=170$ we get $a_2=241$, $a_3=383$, $a_4=766$, $\dots$ Decide whether $a_7$ can be a prime.

cz.2006.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2006.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $m$ and $n$ be positive integers such that the equation $$(x+m)(x+n)=x+m+n$$ has at least one integer solution. Prove that $$\frac{1}{2}<\frac{m}{n}<2.$$

cz.2006.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2006.1.3.reviewed_statement:
In a triangle $ABC$ which is not equilateral, let $K$ be the intersection of the bisector of the interior angle $BAC$ with the side $BC$, and $L$ the intersection of the bisector of the interior angle $ABC$ with the side $AC$. Further, let $S$ be the incentre, $O$ the circumcentre and $V$ the orthocentre of the triangle $ABC$. Prove that the following two statements are equivalent:

a) The line $KL$ is tangent to the circumcircles of the triangles $ALS$, $BVS$ and $BKS$.

b) The points $A$, $B$, $K$, $L$ and $O$ lie on one circle.

cz.2006.2.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2006.2.4.reviewed_statement: A segment $AB$ is given in the plane. Construct the locus of the centroids of all acute triangles $ABC$ with the following property: the vertices $A$ and $B$, the orthocentre $V$ and the incentre $S$ of the triangle $ABC$ lie on one circle.

cz.2006.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2006.2.5.reviewed_statement: Find all triples of pairwise distinct primes $p$, $q$, $r$ satisfying the following conditions: $$\begin{aligned}p&\mid q+r,\\q&\mid r+2p,\\r&\mid p+3q.\end{aligned}$$

cz.2006.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2006.2.6.reviewed_statement: Solve in the set of real numbers the system of equations $$\begin{aligned}\tan^2 x+2\cot^2 2y&=1,\\\tan^2 y+2\cot^2 2z&=1,\\\tan^2 z+2\cot^2 2x&=1.\end{aligned}$$

cz.2007.1.1.scope: Official English wording of the Czech MO booklet compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2007.1.1.reviewed_statement: A chess piece is placed on some square in an $n\times n$ ($n\ge 2$) square chessboard. It then makes alternately “straight” and “diagonal” moves. “Straight” means to a square having a common side with the original square. “Diagonal” means to a square which has exactly one point in common with the original square. Find all $n$ for which there exists a sequence of moves, starting by a “diagonal” move from the original square, such that the piece passes through all squares of the chessboard, and through each square exactly once.

cz.2007.1.2.scope: Official English wording of the Czech MO booklet compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2007.1.2.reviewed_statement: In a chordal quadrangle $ABCD$ denote by $L$, $M$ the incenters of the triangles $BCA$ and $BCD$, respectively. Denote further by $R$ the intersection of the perpendiculars from the points $L$ and $M$ onto the lines $AC$ and $BD$, respectively. Show that the triangle $LMR$ is isosceles.

cz.2007.1.3.scope: Official English wording of the Czech MO booklet compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2007.1.3.reviewed_statement: Denote by $\mathbb{N}$ the set of all natural numbers and consider all functions $f\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ such that for any $x,y\in\mathbb{N}$, $$f\bigl(xf(y)\bigr)=yf(x).$$ Find the least possible value of $f(2007)$.

cz.2007.2.4.scope: Official English wording of the Czech MO booklet compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2007.2.4.reviewed_statement: The set $M$ contains all natural numbers from $1$ to $2007$ (inclusive) and has the following property: if $n\in M$, then $M$ contains all the members of the arithmetic progression with first member $n$ and difference $n+1$. Decide whether there must always exist a number $m$ such that $M$ contains all natural numbers greater than $m$.

cz.2007.2.5.scope: Official English wording of the Czech MO booklet compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2007.2.5.reviewed_statement: An acute triangle $ABC$ is given such that $|AC|\ne|BC|$. In the interior of its sides $BC$ and $AC$ consider the points $D$ and $E$, respectively, for which $ABDE$ is a chordal quadrangle. Denote by $P$ the intersection of its diagonals $AD$ and $BE$. Show that if the lines $CP$ and $AB$ are perpendicular, then $P$ is the orthocenter of the triangle $ABC$.

cz.2007.2.6.scope: Official English wording of the Czech MO booklet compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2007.2.6.reviewed_statement: Find all ordered triples $(x,y,z)$ of mutually distinct real numbers which satisfy the set equation $$\{x,y,z\}=\left\{\frac{x-y}{y-z},\ \frac{y-z}{z-x},\ \frac{z-x}{x-y}\right\}.$$

cz.2008.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2008.1.1.reviewed_statement: Determine the coefficients $p$, $q$, $r$ of the polynomial $f(x)=x^3+px^2+qx+r$ if you know that they are nonzero pairwise distinct integers and that $f(p)=p^3$, $f(q)=q^3$.

cz.2008.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text of the national final (category A) and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cz.2008.1.2.reviewed_statement:
In an acute triangle $ABC$ with $|AC|\ne|BC|$, let $D$ and $E$ be the feet of the altitudes from the vertices $A$ and $B$. Let $V$ be the orthocentre of the triangle $ABC$, $F$ the intersection of the lines $AB$ and $DE$, and $S$ the midpoint of the side $AB$. Further, let $K$ be the intersection of the circumcircles of the triangles $BDS$ and $AES$ different from the point $S$.

a) Prove that the points $D$, $E$, $V$, $K$ lie on one circle.

b) Prove that the points $F$, $V$, $K$ lie on one line.

cz.2008.1.3.reviewed_statement: In an $n\times n$ table, where $n\ge 2$, all the numbers $1,2,\dots,n^2$ are written row by row in this order (the first row contains the numbers $1,2,\dots,n$ in succession, the second row $n+1,n+2,\dots,2n$, etc.). In one step we may choose any two numbers in adjacent cells (i.e. cells having a common side) and either increase both of them by $1$ or decrease both of them by $1$. For which $n$ is it possible to obtain, after a finite number of steps, a table in which all numbers are equal to $365$?

cz.2009.2.4.reviewed_statement:

a) Show that $n=58$ has this property, and find the corresponding four numbers $k$.

b) Show that an even number $n=2p$, where $p\ge 3$, has this property if and only if both $p$ and $2p+1$ are primes.

Decide for which $n$ it is possible to achieve, after a finite number of steps, that for each $k$, $1\le k\le n$, there are exactly $n+1-k$ coins in the vertex $A_k$.

cz.2010.1.3.reviewed_statement:
A wizard kidnapped $31$ members of the political party $A$, $28$ members of the party $B$, $23$ members of the party $C$, and $19$ members of the party $D$ and kept them separately in single cells on his castle and made them to do some work. Each day after the work the party members could walk on the courtyard and talk to each other. But when three members of different parties started to talk to each other, the wizard re-registered them into the fourth party. (More than $3$ kidnapped party members never talked to each other.)

a) Is it possible that after some time all the kidnapped people were members of one political party? Which one?

b) Find all the quadruples of positive integers with the sum $101$ which admit, considered as numbers of kidnapped party members, that after some time they become, with the “help” of the wizard, the members of a single party.

We complete the triangle $ACD$ into the trapezoid $ABCD$ inscribed into $k$. Determine the set of intersection points of lines $BC$ and $AD$ of such trapezoids.

We proceed in this manner until no product of any two numbers on the blackboard is a square. (In one step we may also erase two equal numbers and replace them by the same number.) a) Each of $xy$, $yz$, $zx$ is at least $9$, but at most $25$.

b) Some of $x$, $y$, $z$ is at most $3$, and some at least $5$.

cz.2011.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let us consider a quadratic polynomial $f(x)=ax^2+bx+c$ with real coefficients $a\ge 2$, $b\ge 2$, and $c\ge 2$. Adam and Boris can change the polynomial consecutively in the following game: Adam is allowed in his turn to choose one of coefficients and replace it with the sum of the other two. Boris in his turn can choose one of coefficients and replace it with the product of the other two. They take turns and Adam begins. The winner is the one who succeeds in his turn to change the polynomial into the one with two distinct real roots. Depending on $a$, $b$, and $c$, the coefficients of the original polynomial $f(x)$, determine which of the players has a winning strategy.

cz.2013.1.2.reviewed_statement: Each of the robbers in a band of $n$ members ($n\ge 3$) has plundered a certain number of coins. Altogether $100n$ coins were plundered. The robbers decided to share the loot in the following way: in each step, one of the robbers gives one coin to each of two other robbers. Find all positive integers $n\ge 3$ for which, after a finite number of steps, each robber can have $100$ coins, regardless of how many coins the individual robbers plundered.

cz.2018.1.1.reviewed_statement: In a certain club, some pairs of members are friends. Given $k\ge 3$, we say that a club is $k$-good if every group of $k$ members can be seated around a round table such that every two neighbors are friends. Prove that if a club is $6$-good then it is $7$-good.
