bw.2006.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.2.reviewed_statement: Suppose that the real numbers $a_i\in[-2,17]$, $i=1, 2, \ldots, 59$, satisfy $a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_{59}=0$. Prove that $$a_1^2+a_2^2+\cdots+a_{59}^2\leq 2006.$$

bw.2006.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.3.reviewed_statement: Prove that for every polynomial $P(x)$ with real coefficients there exist a positive integer $m$ and polynomials $P_1(x), \ldots, P_m(x)$ with real coefficients such that $$P(x)=\big(P_1(x)\big)^3+\cdots+\big(P_m(x)\big)^3.$$

bw.2006.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.4.reviewed_statement: Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$, $e$, $f$ be non-negative real numbers satisfying $a+b+c+d+e+f=6$. Find the maximal possible value of $$abc+bcd+cde+def+efa+fab$$ and determine all $6$-tuples $(a,b,c,d,e,f)$ for which this maximal value is achieved.

bw.2006.0.5.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.5.reviewed_statement:
An occasionally unreliable professor has devoted his last book to a certain binary operation $*$. When this operation is applied to any two integers, the result is again an integer. The operation is known to satisfy the following axioms:
(a) $x*(x*y)=y$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$;
(b) $(x*y)*y=x$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$.
The professor claims in his book that
1. the operation $*$ is commutative: $x*y=y*x$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{Z}$;
2. the operation $*$ is associative: $(x*y)*z=x*(y*z)$ for all $x,y,z\in\mathbb{Z}$.
Which of these claims follow from the stated axioms?

bw.2006.0.6.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.6.reviewed_statement:
Determine the maximal size of a set of positive integers with the following properties:
1. The integers consist of digits from the set $\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$.
2. No digit occurs more than once in the same integer.
3. The digits in each integer are in increasing order.
4. Any two integers have at least one digit in common (possibly at different positions).
5. There is no digit which appears in all the integers.

bw.2006.0.7.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.7.reviewed_statement: A photographer took some pictures at a party with $10$ people. Each of the $45$ possible pairs of people appears together on exactly one photo, and each photo depicts two or three people. What is the smallest possible number of photos taken?

bw.2006.0.8.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.8.reviewed_statement: The director has found out that six conspiracies have been set up in his department, each of them involving exactly $3$ persons. Prove that the director can split the department in two laboratories so that none of the conspirative groups is entirely in the same laboratory.

bw.2006.0.9.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.9.reviewed_statement: To every vertex of a regular pentagon a real number is assigned. We may perform the following operation repeatedly: we choose two adjacent vertices of the pentagon and replace each of the two numbers assigned to these vertices by their arithmetic mean. Is it always possible to obtain the position in which all five numbers are zeroes, given that in the initial position the sum of all five numbers is equal to zero?

bw.2006.0.10.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.10.reviewed_statement: $162$ pluses and $144$ minuses are placed in a $30\times 30$ table in such a way that each row and each column contains at most $17$ signs. (No cell contains more than one sign.) For every plus we count the number of minuses in its row and for every minus we count the number of pluses in its column. Find the maximum of the sum of these numbers.

bw.2006.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.11.reviewed_statement: The altitudes of a triangle are $12$, $15$ and $20$. What is the area of this triangle?

bw.2006.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.12.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle, let $B_1$ be the midpoint of the side $AB$ and $C_1$ the midpoint of the side $AC$. Let $P$ be the point of intersection, other than $A$, of the circumscribed circles around the triangles $ABC_1$ and $AB_1C$. Let $P_1$ be the point of intersection, other than $A$, of the line $AP$ with the circumscribed circle around the triangle $AB_1C_1$. Prove that $2AP=3AP_1$.

bw.2006.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.13.reviewed_statement: In a triangle $ABC$, points $D$, $E$ lie on sides $AB$, $AC$ respectively. The lines $BE$ and $CD$ intersect at $F$. Prove that if $$BC^2=BD\cdot BA+CE\cdot CA,$$ then the points $A$, $D$, $F$, $E$ lie on a circle.

bw.2006.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.14.reviewed_statement: There are $2006$ points marked on the surface of a sphere. Prove that the surface can be cut into $2006$ congruent pieces so that each piece contains exactly one of these points inside it.

bw.2006.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.15.reviewed_statement: Let the medians of the triangle $ABC$ intersect at point $M$. A line $t$ through $M$ intersects the circumcircle of $ABC$ at $X$ and $Y$ so that $A$ and $C$ lie on the same side of $t$. Prove that $BX\cdot BY=AX\cdot AY+CX\cdot CY$.

bw.2006.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.16.reviewed_statement: Are there $4$ distinct positive integers such that adding the product of any two of them to $2006$ yields a perfect square?

bw.2006.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.17.reviewed_statement: Determine all positive integers $n$ such that $3^n+1$ is divisible by $n^2$.

bw.2006.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.18.reviewed_statement: For a positive integer $n$ let $a_n$ denote the last digit of $n^{(n^n)}$. Prove that the sequence $(a_n)$ is periodic and determine the length of the minimal period.

bw.2006.0.19.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.19.reviewed_statement: Does there exist a sequence $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$ of positive integers such that the sum of every $n$ consecutive elements is divisible by $n^2$ for every positive integer $n$?

bw.2006.0.20.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2006.0.20.reviewed_statement: A $12$-digit positive integer consisting only of digits $1$, $5$ and $9$ is divisible by $37$. Prove that the sum of its digits is not equal to $76$.

bw.2007.0.1.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.1.reviewed_statement: For a positive integer $n$ consider any partition of the set $\{1, 2, \ldots, 2n\}$ into $n$ two-element subsets $P_1, P_2, \ldots, P_n$. In each subset $P_i$, let $p_i$ be the product of the two numbers in $P_i$. Prove that $$\frac{1}{p_1}+\frac{1}{p_2}+\cdots+\frac{1}{p_n}<1.$$

bw.2007.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.2.reviewed_statement: A sequence of integers $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$ is called exact if $a_n^2-a_m^2=a_{n-m}a_{n+m}$ for any $n>m$. Prove that there exists an exact sequence with $a_1=1$, $a_2=0$ and determine $a_{2007}$.

bw.2007.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.

bw.2007.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.4.reviewed_statement: Let $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ be positive real numbers, and let $S=a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_n$. Prove that $$(2S+n)(2S+a_1a_2+a_2a_3+\cdots+a_na_1)\geq 9\left(\sqrt{a_1a_2}+\sqrt{a_2a_3}+\cdots+\sqrt{a_na_1}\right)^2.$$

bw.2007.0.5.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.5.reviewed_statement: A function $f$ is defined on the set of all real numbers except $0$ and takes all real values except $1$. It is also known that $$f(xy)=f(x)f(-y)-f(x)+f(y)$$ for any $x,y\neq 0$ and that $$f\big(f(x)\big)=\frac{1}{f\left(\frac1x\right)}$$ for any $x\notin\{0,1\}$. Determine all such functions $f$.

bw.2007.0.6.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.6.reviewed_statement: Freddy writes down numbers $1, 2, \ldots, n$ in some order. Then he makes a list of all pairs $(i,j)$ such that $1\leq i<j\leq n$ and the $i$-th number is bigger than the $j$-th number in his permutation. After that, Freddy repeats the following action while possible: choose a pair $(i,j)$ from the current list, interchange the $i$-th and the $j$-th number in the current permutation, and delete $(i,j)$ from the list. Prove that Freddy can choose pairs in such an order that, after the process finishes, the numbers in the permutation are in ascending order.

bw.2007.0.7.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.7.reviewed_statement:
A squiggle is composed of six regular triangles with side length $1$ as shown in the figure below. Determine all possible integers $n$ such that a regular triangle with side length $n$ can be fully covered with squiggles (rotations and reflections of squiggles are allowed, overlappings are not).

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/bw_2007_p7_fig.png

bw.2007.0.8.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.8.reviewed_statement: Call a set $A$ of integers non-isolated if for every $a\in A$ at least one of the numbers $a-1$ and $a+1$ also belongs to $A$. Prove that the number of five-element non-isolated subsets of $\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$ is $(n-4)^2$.

bw.2007.0.9.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.9.reviewed_statement: A society has to elect a board of governors. Each member of the society has chosen $10$ candidates for the board, but he will be happy if at least one of them will be on the board. For each six members of the society there exists a board consisting of two persons making all of these six members happy. Prove that a board consisting of $10$ persons can be elected making every member of the society happy.

bw.2007.0.10.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.10.reviewed_statement: We are given an $18\times 18$ table, all of whose cells may be black or white. Initially all the cells are coloured white. We may perform the following operation: choose one column or one row and change the colour of all cells in this column or row. Is it possible by repeating the operation to obtain a table with exactly $16$ black cells?

bw.2007.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.

bw.2007.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.12.reviewed_statement: Let $M$ be a point on the arc $AB$ of the circumcircle of the triangle $ABC$ which does not contain $C$. Suppose that the projections of $M$ onto the lines $AB$ and $BC$ lie on the sides themselves, not on their extensions. Denote these projections by $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Let $K$ and $N$ be the midpoints of $AC$ and $XY$, respectively. Prove that $\angle MNK=90^\circ$.

bw.2007.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.13.reviewed_statement: Let $t_1, t_2, \ldots, t_k$ be different straight lines in space, where $k>1$. Prove that points $P_i$ on $t_i$, $i=1, \ldots, k$, exist such that $P_{i+1}$ is the projection of $P_i$ on $t_{i+1}$ for $i=1, \ldots, k-1$, and $P_1$ is the projection of $P_k$ on $t_1$.

bw.2007.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.14.reviewed_statement: In a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ we have $\angle ADC=90^\circ$. Let $E$ and $F$ be the projections of $B$ onto the lines $AD$ and $AC$, respectively. Assume that $F$ lies between $A$ and $C$, that $A$ lies between $D$ and $E$, and that the line $EF$ passes through the midpoint of the segment $BD$. Prove that the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is cyclic.

bw.2007.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.15.reviewed_statement: The incircle of the triangle $ABC$ touches the side $AC$ at the point $D$. Another circle passes through $D$ and touches the rays $BC$ and $BA$, the latter at the point $A$. Determine the ratio $\frac{AD}{DC}$.

bw.2007.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.16.reviewed_statement: Let $a$ and $b$ be rational numbers such that $s=a+b=a^2+b^2$. Prove that $s$ can be written as a fraction where the denominator is relatively prime to $6$.

bw.2007.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.17.reviewed_statement: Let $x$, $y$, $z$ be positive integers such that $\frac{x+1}{y}+\frac{y+1}{z}+\frac{z+1}{x}$ is an integer. Let $d$ be the greatest common divisor of $x$, $y$ and $z$. Prove that $d\leq\sqrt[3]{xy+yz+zx}$.

bw.2007.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.18.reviewed_statement: Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ be non-zero integers, such that the only quadruple of integers $(x,y,z,t)$ satisfying the equation $$ax^2+by^2+cz^2+dt^2=0$$ is $x=y=z=t=0$. Does it follow that the numbers $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ have the same sign?

bw.2007.0.19.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.19.reviewed_statement: Let $r$ and $k$ be positive integers such that all prime divisors of $r$ are greater than $50$. A positive integer, whose decimal representation (without leading zeroes) has at least $k$ digits, will be called nice if every sequence of $k$ consecutive digits of this decimal representation forms a number (possibly with leading zeroes) which is a multiple of $r$. Prove that if there exist infinitely many nice numbers, then the number $10^k-1$ is nice as well.

bw.2007.0.20.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2007.0.20.reviewed_statement: Let $a$ and $b$ be positive integers, $b<a$, such that $a^3+b^3+ab$ is divisible by $ab(a-b)$. Prove that $ab$ is a perfect cube.

bw.2008.0.1.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.1.reviewed_statement: Determine all polynomials $p(x)$ with real coefficients such that $p\big((x+1)^3\big)=\big(p(x)+1\big)^3$ and $p(0)=0$.

bw.2008.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.2.reviewed_statement: Prove that if the real numbers $a$, $b$ and $c$ satisfy $a^2+b^2+c^2=3$ then $$\frac{a^2}{2+b+c^2}+\frac{b^2}{2+c+a^2}+\frac{c^2}{2+a+b^2}\geq\frac{(a+b+c)^2}{12}.$$ When does equality hold?

bw.2008.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.3.reviewed_statement: Does there exist an angle $\alpha\in(0,\pi/2)$ such that $\sin\alpha$, $\cos\alpha$, $\tan\alpha$ and $\cot\alpha$, taken in some order, are consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression?

bw.2008.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.4.reviewed_statement: The polynomial $P$ has integer coefficients and $P(x)=5$ for five different integers $x$. Show that there is no integer $x$ such that $-6\leq P(x)\leq 4$ or $6\leq P(x)\leq 16$.

bw.2008.0.5.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.5.reviewed_statement: Suppose that Romeo and Juliet each have a regular tetrahedron to the vertices of which some positive real numbers are assigned. They associate each edge of their tetrahedra with the product of the two numbers assigned to its end points. Then they write on each face of their tetrahedra the sum of the three numbers associated to its three edges. The four numbers written on the faces of Romeo's tetrahedron turn out to coincide with the four numbers written on Juliet's tetrahedron. Does it follow that the four numbers assigned to the vertices of Romeo's tetrahedron are identical to the four numbers assigned to the vertices of Juliet's tetrahedron?

bw.2008.0.6.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.6.reviewed_statement: Find all finite sets of positive integers with at least two elements such that for any two numbers $a$, $b$ ($a>b$) belonging to the set, the number $\frac{b^2}{a-b}$ belongs to the set, too.

bw.2008.0.7.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.7.reviewed_statement: How many pairs $(m,n)$ of positive integers with $m<n$ fulfill the equation $$\frac{3}{2008}=\frac1m+\frac1n?$$

bw.2008.0.8.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.8.reviewed_statement: Consider a set $A$ of positive integers such that the least element of $A$ equals $1001$ and the product of all elements of $A$ is a perfect square. What is the least possible value of the greatest element of $A$?

bw.2008.0.9.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.9.reviewed_statement: Suppose that the positive integers $a$ and $b$ satisfy the equation $$a^b-b^a=1008.$$ Prove that $a$ and $b$ are congruent modulo $1008$.

bw.2008.0.10.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.10.reviewed_statement: For a positive integer $n$, let $S(n)$ denote the sum of its digits. Find the largest possible value of the expression $\frac{S(n)}{S(16n)}$.

bw.2008.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.11.reviewed_statement: Consider a subset $A$ of $84$ elements of the set $\{1, 2, \ldots, 169\}$ such that no two elements in the set add up to $169$. Show that $A$ contains a perfect square.

bw.2008.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.12.reviewed_statement: In a school class with $3n$ children, any two children make a common present to exactly one other child. Prove that for all odd $n$ it is possible that the following holds: for any three children $A$, $B$ and $C$ in the class, if $A$ and $B$ make a present to $C$ then $A$ and $C$ make a present to $B$.

bw.2008.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.

bw.2008.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.14.reviewed_statement:
Is it possible to build a $4\times 4\times 4$ cube from blocks of the following shape consisting of $4$ unit cubes?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/bw_2008_p14_fig.png

bw.2008.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.15.reviewed_statement: Some $1\times 2$ dominoes, each covering two adjacent unit squares, are placed on a board of size $n\times n$ such that no two of them touch (not even at a corner). Given that the total area covered by the dominoes is $2008$, find the least possible value of $n$.

bw.2008.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.16.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram. The circle with diameter $AC$ intersects the line $BD$ at points $P$ and $Q$. The perpendicular to the line $AC$ passing through the point $C$ intersects the lines $AB$ and $AD$ at points $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Prove that the points $P$, $Q$, $X$ and $Y$ lie on the same circle.

bw.2008.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.17.reviewed_statement: Assume that $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ are the sides of a quadrilateral inscribed in a given circle. Prove that the product $(ab+cd)(ac+bd)(ad+bc)$ acquires its maximum when the quadrilateral is a square.

bw.2008.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.18.reviewed_statement: Let $AB$ be a diameter of a circle $S$, and let $L$ be the tangent at $A$. Furthermore, let $c$ be a fixed, positive real, and consider all pairs of points $X$ and $Y$ lying on $L$, on opposite sides of $A$, such that $|AX|\cdot|AY|=c$. The lines $BX$ and $BY$ intersect $S$ at points $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Show that all the lines $PQ$ pass through a common point.

bw.2008.0.19.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.19.reviewed_statement: In a circle of diameter $1$, some chords are drawn. The sum of their lengths is greater than $19$. Prove that there is a diameter intersecting at least $7$ chords.

bw.2008.0.20.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2008.0.20.reviewed_statement: Let $M$ be a point on $BC$ and $N$ be a point on $AB$ such that $AM$ and $CN$ are angle bisectors of the triangle $ABC$. Given that $$\frac{\angle BNM}{\angle MNC}=\frac{\angle BMN}{\angle NMA},$$ prove that the triangle $ABC$ is isosceles.

bw.2009.0.1.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.1.reviewed_statement: A polynomial $p(x)$ of degree $n\geq 2$ has exactly $n$ real roots, counted with multiplicity. We know that the coefficient of $x^n$ is $1$, all the roots are less than or equal to $1$, and $p(2)=3^n$. What values can $p(1)$ take?

bw.2009.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{100}$ be nonnegative integers satisfying the inequality $$\begin{aligned}&a_1(a_1-1)\cdots(a_1-20)+a_2(a_2-1)\cdots(a_2-20)+\cdots\\&+a_{100}(a_{100}-1)\cdots(a_{100}-20)\leq 100\cdot 99\cdot 98\cdots 79.\end{aligned}$$ Prove that $a_1+a_2+\cdots+a_{100}\leq 9900$.

bw.2009.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.3.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a given positive integer. Show that we can choose numbers $c_k\in\{-1,1\}$ ($1\leq k\leq n$) such that $$0\leq\sum_{k=1}^{n}c_k\cdot k^2\leq 4.$$

bw.2009.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.4.reviewed_statement: Determine all integers $n>1$ for which the inequality $$x_1^2+x_2^2+\cdots+x_n^2\geq(x_1+x_2+\cdots+x_{n-1})x_n$$ holds for all real $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$.

bw.2009.0.5.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.5.reviewed_statement: Let $f_0=f_1=1$ and $f_{i+2}=f_{i+1}+f_i$ for all $i\geq 0$. Find all real solutions to the equation $$x^{2010}=f_{2009}\cdot x+f_{2008}.$$

bw.2009.0.6.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.6.reviewed_statement: Let $a$ and $b$ be integers such that the equation $x^3-ax^2-b=0$ has three integer roots. Prove that $b=dk^2$, where $d$ and $k$ are integers and $d$ divides $a$.

bw.2009.0.7.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.7.reviewed_statement: Suppose that for a prime number $p$ and integers $a$, $b$, $c$ the following holds: $$6\mid p+1,\quad p\mid a+b+c,\quad p\mid a^4+b^4+c^4.$$ Prove that $p$ divides each of $a$, $b$, $c$.

bw.2009.0.8.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.8.reviewed_statement: Determine all positive integers $n$ for which there exists a partition of the set $$\{n, n+1, n+2, \ldots, n+8\}$$ into two subsets such that the product of all elements of the first subset is equal to the product of all elements of the second subset.

bw.2009.0.9.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.9.reviewed_statement: Determine all positive integers $n$ for which $2^{n+1}-n^2$ is a prime number.

bw.2009.0.10.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.10.reviewed_statement: Let $d(k)$ denote the number of positive divisors of a positive integer $k$. Prove that there exist infinitely many positive integers $M$ that cannot be written as $$M=\left(\frac{2\sqrt{n}}{d(n)}\right)^2$$ for any positive integer $n$.

bw.2009.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.11.reviewed_statement: Let $M$ be the midpoint of the side $AC$ of a triangle $ABC$, and let $K$ be a point on the ray $BA$ beyond $A$. The line $KM$ intersects the side $BC$ at the point $L$. $P$ is the point on the segment $BM$ such that $PM$ is the bisector of the angle $LPK$. The line $\ell$ passes through $A$ and is parallel to $BM$. Prove that the projection of the point $M$ onto the line $\ell$ belongs to the line $PK$.

bw.2009.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.12.reviewed_statement: In a quadrilateral $ABCD$ we have $AB\parallel CD$ and $AB=2CD$. A line $\ell$ is perpendicular to $CD$ and contains the point $C$. The circle with centre $D$ and radius $DA$ intersects the line $\ell$ at points $P$ and $Q$. Prove that $AP\perp BQ$.

bw.2009.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.13.reviewed_statement: The point $H$ is the orthocentre of a triangle $ABC$, and the segments $AD$, $BE$, $CF$ are its altitudes. The points $I_1$, $I_2$, $I_3$ are the incentres of the triangles $EHF$, $FHD$, $DHE$ respectively. Prove that the lines $AI_1$, $BI_2$, $CI_3$ intersect at a single point.

bw.2009.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.14.reviewed_statement: For which $n\geq 2$ is it possible to find $n$ pairwise non-similar triangles $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$ such that each of them can be divided into $n$ pairwise non-similar triangles, each of them similar to one of $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$?

bw.2009.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.15.reviewed_statement: A unit square is cut into $m$ quadrilaterals $Q_1, \ldots, Q_m$. For each $i=1, \ldots, m$ let $S_i$ be the sum of the squares of the four sides of $Q_i$. Prove that $$S_1+\cdots+S_m\geq 4.$$

bw.2009.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.16.reviewed_statement: An $n$-trønder walk is a walk starting at $(0,0)$, ending at $(2n,0)$ with no self intersection and not leaving the first quadrant, where every step is one of the vectors $(1,1)$, $(1,-1)$ or $(-1,1)$. Find the number of $n$-trønder walks.

bw.2009.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.17.reviewed_statement: Find the largest integer $n$ for which there exist $n$ different integers such that none of them are divisible by either of $7$, $11$ or $13$, but the sum of any two of them is divisible by at least one of $7$, $11$ and $13$.

bw.2009.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.18.reviewed_statement: Let $n>2$ be an integer. In a country there are $n$ cities and every two of them are connected by a direct road. Each road is assigned an integer from the set $\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$ (different roads may be assigned the same number). The priority of a city is the sum of the numbers assigned to roads which lead to it. Find the smallest $m$ for which it is possible that all cities have a different priority.

bw.2009.0.19.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.

bw.2009.0.20.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2009.0.20.reviewed_statement: In the future city Baltic Way there are sixteen hospitals. Every night exactly four of them must be on duty for emergencies. Is it possible to arrange the schedule in such a way that after twenty nights every pair of hospitals have been on common duty exactly once?

bw.2010.0.1.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.1.reviewed_statement: Find all quadruples of real numbers $(a,b,c,d)$ satisfying the system of equations $$\begin{cases}(b+c+d)^{2010}=3a\\ (a+c+d)^{2010}=3b\\ (a+b+d)^{2010}=3c\\ (a+b+c)^{2010}=3d.\end{cases}$$

bw.2010.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $x$ be a real number such that $0<x<\frac{\pi}{2}$. Prove that $$\cos^2(x)\cot(x)+\sin^2(x)\tan(x)\geq 1.$$

bw.2010.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.3.reviewed_statement: Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$ ($n\geq 2$) be real numbers greater than $1$. Suppose that $|x_i-x_{i+1}|<1$ for $i=1, 2, \ldots, n-1$. Prove that $$\frac{x_1}{x_2}+\frac{x_2}{x_3}+\cdots+\frac{x_{n-1}}{x_n}+\frac{x_n}{x_1}<2n-1.$$

bw.2010.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.4.reviewed_statement: Find all polynomials $P(x)$ with real coefficients such that $$(x-2010)P(x+67)=xP(x)$$ for every integer $x$.

bw.2010.0.5.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.5.reviewed_statement: Let $\mathbb{R}$ denote the set of real numbers. Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $$f(x^2)+f(xy)=f(x)f(y)+yf(x)+xf(x+y)$$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$.

bw.2010.0.6.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.6.reviewed_statement: An $n\times n$ board is coloured in $n$ colours such that the main diagonal (from top-left to bottom-right) is coloured in the first colour; the two adjacent diagonals are coloured in the second colour; the two next diagonals (one from above and one from below) are coloured in the third colour, etc.; the two corners (top-right and bottom-left) are coloured in the $n$-th colour. It happens that it is possible to place on the board $n$ rooks, no two attacking each other and such that no two rooks stand on cells of the same colour. Prove that $n\equiv 0\pmod 4$ or $n\equiv 1\pmod 4$.

bw.2010.0.7.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.7.reviewed_statement: There are some cities in a country; one of them is the capital. For any two cities $A$ and $B$ there is a direct flight from $A$ to $B$ and a direct flight from $B$ to $A$, both having the same price. Suppose that all round trips with exactly one landing in every city have the same total cost. Prove that all round trips that miss the capital and with exactly one landing in every remaining city cost the same.

bw.2010.0.8.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.8.reviewed_statement: In a club with $30$ members, every member initially had a hat. One day each member sent his hat to a different member (a member could have received more than one hat). Prove that there exists a group of $10$ members such that no one in the group has received a hat from another one in the group.

bw.2010.0.9.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.9.reviewed_statement: There is a pile of $1000$ matches. Two players each take turns and can take $1$ to $5$ matches. It is also allowed at most $10$ times during the whole game to take $6$ matches, for example $7$ exceptional moves can be done by the first player and $3$ moves by the second and then no more exceptional moves are allowed. Whoever takes the last match wins. Determine which player has a winning strategy.

bw.2010.0.10.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.10.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be an integer with $n\geq 3$. Consider all dissections of a convex $n$-gon into triangles by $n-3$ non-intersecting diagonals, and all colourings of the triangles with black and white so that triangles with a common side are always of a different colour. Find the least possible number of black triangles.

bw.2010.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.11.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a square and let $S$ be the point of intersection of its diagonals $AC$ and $BD$. Two circles $k$, $k'$ go through $A$, $C$ and $B$, $D$, respectively. Furthermore, $k$ and $k'$ intersect in exactly two different points $P$ and $Q$. Prove that $S$ lies on $PQ$.

bw.2010.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.12.reviewed_statement:
Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral with precisely one pair of parallel sides.
(a) Show that the lengths of its sides $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DA$ (in this order) do not form an arithmetic progression.
(b) Show that there is such a quadrilateral for which the lengths of its sides $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DA$ form an arithmetic progression after the order of the lengths is changed.

bw.2010.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.13.reviewed_statement: In an acute triangle $ABC$, the segment $CD$ is an altitude and $H$ is the orthocentre. Given that the circumcentre of the triangle lies on the line containing the bisector of the angle $DHB$, determine all possible values of $\angle CAB$.

bw.2010.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.14.reviewed_statement: Assume that all angles of a triangle $ABC$ are acute. Let $D$ and $E$ be points on the sides $AC$ and $BC$ of the triangle such that $A$, $B$, $D$ and $E$ lie on the same circle. Further suppose the circle through $D$, $E$ and $C$ intersects the side $AB$ in two points $X$ and $Y$. Show that the midpoint of $XY$ is the foot of the altitude from $C$ to $AB$.

bw.2010.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.15.reviewed_statement: The points $M$ and $N$ are chosen on the angle bisector $AL$ of a triangle $ABC$ such that $\angle ABM=\angle ACN=23^\circ$. $X$ is a point inside the triangle such that $BX=CX$ and $\angle BXC=2\angle BML$. Find $\angle MXN$.

bw.2010.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.16.reviewed_statement: For a positive integer $k$, let $d(k)$ denote the number of divisors of $k$ and let $s(k)$ denote the digit sum of $k$. A positive integer $n$ is said to be amusing if there exists a positive integer $k$ such that $d(k)=s(k)=n$. What is the smallest amusing odd integer greater than $1$?

bw.2010.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.17.reviewed_statement: Find all positive integers $n$ such that the decimal representation of $n^2$ consists of odd digits only.

bw.2010.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.18.reviewed_statement: Let $p$ be a prime number. For each $k$, $1\leq k\leq p-1$, there exists a unique integer denoted by $k^{-1}$ such that $1\leq k^{-1}\leq p-1$ and $k^{-1}\cdot k\equiv 1\pmod p$. Prove that the sequence $$1^{-1},\quad 1^{-1}+2^{-1},\quad 1^{-1}+2^{-1}+3^{-1},\quad\ldots,\quad 1^{-1}+2^{-1}+\cdots+(p-1)^{-1}$$ (addition modulo $p$) contains at most $\frac{p+1}{2}$ distinct elements.

bw.2010.0.19.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.19.reviewed_statement: For which $k$ do there exist $k$ pairwise distinct primes $p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_k$ such that $$p_1^2+p_2^2+\cdots+p_k^2=2010?$$

bw.2010.0.20.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2010.0.20.reviewed_statement: Determine all positive integers $n$ for which there exists an infinite subset $A$ of the set $\mathbb{N}$ of positive integers such that for all pairwise distinct $a_1, \ldots, a_n\in A$ the numbers $a_1+\cdots+a_n$ and $a_1a_2\cdots a_n$ are coprime.

bw.2011.0.1.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.1.reviewed_statement: The real numbers $x_1, \ldots, x_{2011}$ satisfy $$x_1+x_2=2x_1',\quad x_2+x_3=2x_2',\quad\ldots,\quad x_{2011}+x_1=2x_{2011}',$$ where $x_1', x_2', \ldots, x_{2011}'$ is a permutation of $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{2011}$. Prove that $x_1=x_2=\cdots=x_{2011}$.

bw.2011.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $f:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be a function such that for all integers $x$ and $y$, the following holds: $$f\big(f(x)-y\big)=f(y)-f\big(f(x)\big).$$ Show that $f$ is bounded.

bw.2011.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.3.reviewed_statement: A sequence $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$ of non-negative integers is such that $a_{n+1}$ is the last digit of $a_n^n+a_{n-1}$ for all $n>2$. Is it always true that for some $n_0$ the sequence $a_{n_0}, a_{n_0+1}, a_{n_0+2}, \ldots$ is periodic?

bw.2011.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.4.reviewed_statement: Let $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ be non-negative reals such that $a+b+c+d=4$. Prove the inequality $$\frac{a}{a^3+8}+\frac{b}{b^3+8}+\frac{c}{c^3+8}+\frac{d}{d^3+8}\leq\frac49.$$

bw.2011.0.5.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.5.reviewed_statement: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a function such that $$f\big(f(x)\big)=x^2-x+1$$ for all real numbers $x$. Determine $f(0)$.

bw.2011.0.6.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.6.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Prove that the number of lines which go through the origin and precisely one other point with integer coordinates $(x,y)$, $0\leq x,y\leq n$, is at least $\frac{n^2}{4}$.

bw.2011.0.7.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.7.reviewed_statement: Let $T$ denote the $15$-element set $\{10a+b : a,b\in\mathbb{Z},\ 1\leq a<b\leq 6\}$. Let $S$ be a subset of $T$ in which all six digits $1, 2, \ldots, 6$ appear and in which no three elements together use all these six digits. Determine the largest possible size of $S$.

bw.2011.0.8.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.

bw.2011.0.9.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.

bw.2011.0.10.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.10.reviewed_statement: Two persons play the following game with integers. The initial number is $2011^{2011}$. The players move in turns. Each move consists of subtraction of an integer between $1$ and $2010$ inclusive, or division by $2011$, rounding down to the closest integer when necessary. The player who first obtains a non-positive integer wins. Which player has a winning strategy?

bw.2011.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.11.reviewed_statement: Let $AB$ and $CD$ be two diameters of the circle $\mathcal{C}$. For an arbitrary point $P$ on $\mathcal{C}$, let $R$ and $S$ be the feet of the perpendiculars from $P$ to $AB$ and $CD$, respectively. Show that the length of $RS$ is independent of the choice of $P$.

bw.2011.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.12.reviewed_statement: Let $P$ be a point inside a square $ABCD$ such that $PA:PB:PC$ is $1:2:3$. Determine the angle $\angle BPA$.

bw.2011.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.13.reviewed_statement: Let $E$ be an interior point of the convex quadrilateral $ABCD$. Construct triangles $ABF$, $BCG$, $CDH$ and $DAI$ on the outside of the quadrilateral such that the similarities $\triangle ABF\sim\triangle DCE$, $\triangle BCG\sim\triangle ADE$, $\triangle CDH\sim\triangle BAE$ and $\triangle DAI\sim\triangle CBE$ hold. Let $P$, $Q$, $R$ and $S$ be the projections of $E$ on the lines $AB$, $BC$, $CD$ and $DA$, respectively. Prove that if the quadrilateral $PQRS$ is cyclic, then $$EF\cdot CD=EG\cdot DA=EH\cdot AB=EI\cdot BC.$$

bw.2011.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.14.reviewed_statement: The incircle of a triangle $ABC$ touches the sides $BC$, $CA$, $AB$ at $D$, $E$, $F$, respectively. Let $G$ be a point on the incircle such that $FG$ is a diameter. The lines $EG$ and $FD$ intersect at $H$. Prove that $CH\parallel AB$.

bw.2011.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.15.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral such that $\angle ADB=\angle BDC$. Suppose that a point $E$ on the side $AD$ satisfies the equality $$AE\cdot ED+BE^2=CD\cdot AE.$$ Show that $\angle EBA=\angle DCB$.

bw.2011.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.16.reviewed_statement: Let $a$ be any integer. Define the sequence $x_0, x_1, \ldots$ by $x_0=a$, $x_1=3$, and for all $n>1$ $$x_n=2x_{n-1}-4x_{n-2}+3.$$ Determine the largest integer $k_a$ for which there exists a prime $p$ such that $p^{k_a}$ divides $x_{2011}-1$.

bw.2011.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.17.reviewed_statement: Determine all positive integers $d$ such that whenever $d$ divides a positive integer $n$, $d$ will also divide any integer obtained by rearranging the digits of $n$.

bw.2011.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.18.reviewed_statement: Determine all pairs $(p,q)$ of primes for which both $p^2+q^3$ and $q^2+p^3$ are perfect squares.

bw.2011.0.19.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.19.reviewed_statement: Let $p\neq 3$ be a prime number. Show that there is a non-constant arithmetic sequence of positive integers $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_p$ such that the product of the terms of the sequence is a cube.

bw.2011.0.20.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2011.0.20.reviewed_statement: An integer $n\geq 1$ is called balanced if it has an even number of distinct prime divisors. Prove that there exist infinitely many positive integers $n$ such that there are exactly two balanced numbers among $n$, $n+1$, $n+2$ and $n+3$.

bw.2012.0.1.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.1.reviewed_statement:
The numbers from $1$ to $360$ are partitioned into $9$ subsets of consecutive integers and the sums of the numbers in each subset are arranged in the cells of a $3\times 3$ square. Is it possible that the square turns out to be a magic square?
Remark: A magic square is a square in which the sums of the numbers in each row, in each column and in both diagonals are all equal.

bw.2012.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $a$, $b$, $c$ be real numbers. Prove that $$ab+bc+ca+\max\{|a-b|, |b-c|, |c-a|\}\leq 1+\frac13(a+b+c)^2.$$

bw.2012.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.3.reviewed_statement:
(a) Show that the equation $$\lfloor x\rfloor(x^2+1)=x^3,$$ where $\lfloor x\rfloor$ denotes the largest integer not larger than $x$, has exactly one real solution in each interval between consecutive positive integers.
(b) Show that none of the positive real solutions of this equation is rational.

bw.2012.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.4.reviewed_statement: Prove that for infinitely many pairs $(a,b)$ of integers the equation $$x^{2012}=ax+b$$ has among its solutions two distinct real numbers whose product is $1$.

bw.2012.0.5.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.5.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ for which $$f(x+y)=f(x-y)+f\big(f(1-xy)\big)$$ holds for all real numbers $x$ and $y$.

bw.2012.0.6.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.6.reviewed_statement: There are $2012$ lamps arranged on a table. Two persons play the following game. In each move the player flips the switch of one lamp, but he must never get back an arrangement of the lit lamps that has already been on the table. A player who cannot move loses. Which player has a winning strategy?

bw.2012.0.7.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.7.reviewed_statement: On a $2012\times 2012$ board, some cells on the top-right to bottom-left diagonal are marked. None of the marked cells is in a corner. Integers are written in each cell of this board in the following way. All the numbers in the cells along the upper and the left sides of the board are $1$'s. All the numbers in the marked cells are $0$'s. Each of the other cells contains a number that is equal to the sum of its upper neighbour and its left neighbour. Prove that the number in the bottom right corner is not divisible by $2011$.

bw.2012.0.8.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.8.reviewed_statement: A directed graph does not contain directed cycles. The number of edges in any directed path does not exceed $99$. Prove that it is possible to colour the edges of the graph in $2$ colours so that the number of edges in any single-coloured directed path in the graph will not exceed $9$.

bw.2012.0.9.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.9.reviewed_statement: Zeroes are written in all cells of a $5\times 5$ board. We can take an arbitrary cell and increase by $1$ the number in this cell and all cells having a common side with it. Is it possible to obtain the number $2012$ in all cells simultaneously?

bw.2012.0.10.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.10.reviewed_statement:
Two players $A$ and $B$ play the following game. Before the game starts, $A$ chooses $1000$ not necessarily different odd primes, and then $B$ chooses half of them and writes them on a blackboard. In each turn a player chooses a positive integer $n$, erases some primes $p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n$ from the blackboard and writes all the prime factors of $p_1p_2\cdots p_n-2$ instead (if a prime occurs several times in the prime factorization of $p_1p_2\cdots p_n-2$, it is written as many times as it occurs). Player $A$ starts, and the player whose move leaves the blackboard empty loses the game. Prove that one of the two players has a winning strategy and determine who.
Remark: Since $1$ has no prime factors, erasing a single $3$ is a legal move.

bw.2012.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.11.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with $\angle A=60^\circ$. The point $T$ lies inside the triangle in such a way that $\angle ATB=\angle BTC=\angle CTA=120^\circ$. Let $M$ be the midpoint of $BC$. Prove that $TA+TB+TC=2AM$.

bw.2012.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.12.reviewed_statement: Let $P_0, P_1, \ldots, P_8=P_0$ be successive points on a circle and $Q$ be a point inside the polygon $P_0P_1\cdots P_7$ such that $\angle P_{i-1}QP_i=45^\circ$ for $i=1, \ldots, 8$. Prove that the sum $$\sum_{i=1}^{8}P_{i-1}P_i^2$$ is minimal if and only if $Q$ is the centre of the circle.

bw.2012.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.13.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be an acute triangle, and let $H$ be its orthocentre. Denote by $H_A$, $H_B$ and $H_C$ the second intersection of the circumcircle with the altitudes from $A$, $B$ and $C$ respectively. Prove that the area of triangle $H_AH_BH_C$ does not exceed the area of triangle $ABC$.

bw.2012.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.14.reviewed_statement: Given a triangle $ABC$, let its incircle touch the sides $BC$, $CA$, $AB$ at $D$, $E$, $F$, respectively. Let $G$ be the midpoint of the segment $DE$. Prove that $\angle EFC=\angle GFD$.

bw.2012.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.15.reviewed_statement: The circumcentre $O$ of a given cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ lies inside the quadrilateral but not on the diagonal $AC$. The diagonals of the quadrilateral intersect at $I$. The circumcircle of the triangle $AOI$ meets the sides $AD$ and $AB$ at points $P$ and $Q$, respectively; the circumcircle of the triangle $COI$ meets the sides $CB$ and $CD$ at points $R$ and $S$, respectively. Prove that $PQRS$ is a parallelogram.

bw.2012.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.16.reviewed_statement: Let $n$, $m$ and $k$ be positive integers satisfying $(n-1)n(n+1)=m^k$. Prove that $k=1$.

bw.2012.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.17.reviewed_statement: Let $d(n)$ denote the number of positive divisors of $n$. Find all triples $(n,k,p)$, where $n$ and $k$ are positive integers and $p$ is a prime number, such that $$n^{d(n)}-1=p^k.$$

bw.2012.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.18.reviewed_statement: Find all triples $(a,b,c)$ of integers satisfying $a^2+b^2+c^2=20122012$.

bw.2012.0.19.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.19.reviewed_statement: Show that $n^n+(n+1)^{n+1}$ is composite for infinitely many positive integers $n$.

bw.2012.0.20.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2012.0.20.reviewed_statement: Find all integer solutions of the equation $2x^6+y^7=11$.

bw.2013.0.1.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.1.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Assume that $n$ numbers are to be chosen from the table $$\begin{array}{cccc}0 & 1 & \cdots & n-1\\ n & n+1 & \cdots & 2n-1\\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots\\ (n-1)n & (n-1)n+1 & \cdots & n^2-1\end{array}$$ with no two of them from the same row or the same column. Find the maximal value of the product of these $n$ numbers.

bw.2013.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $k$ and $n$ be positive integers and let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_k, y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_n$ be distinct integers. A polynomial $P$ with integer coefficients satisfies $$P(x_1)=P(x_2)=\cdots=P(x_k)=54,$$ $$P(y_1)=P(y_2)=\cdots=P(y_n)=2013.$$ Determine the maximal value of $kn$.

bw.2013.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.3.reviewed_statement: Let $\mathbb{R}$ denote the set of real numbers. Find all functions $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $$f\big(xf(y)+y\big)+f\big(-f(x)\big)=f\big(yf(x)-y\big)+y$$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$.

bw.2013.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.4.reviewed_statement: Prove that the following inequality holds for all positive real numbers $x$, $y$, $z$: $$\frac{x^3}{y^2+z^2}+\frac{y^3}{z^2+x^2}+\frac{z^3}{x^2+y^2}\geq\frac{x+y+z}{2}.$$

bw.2013.0.5.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.5.reviewed_statement: Numbers $0$ and $2013$ are written at two opposite vertices of a cube. Some real numbers are to be written at the remaining $6$ vertices of the cube. On each edge of the cube the difference between the numbers at its endpoints is written. When is the sum of squares of the numbers written on the edges minimal?

bw.2013.0.6.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.6.reviewed_statement: Santa Claus has at least $n$ gifts for $n$ children. For $i\in\{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, the $i$-th child considers $x_i>0$ of these items to be desirable. Assume that $$\frac{1}{x_1}+\cdots+\frac{1}{x_n}\leq 1.$$ Prove that Santa Claus can give each child a gift that this child likes.

bw.2013.0.7.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.7.reviewed_statement: A positive integer is written on a blackboard. Players $A$ and $B$ play the following game: in each move one has to choose a proper divisor $m$ of the number $n$ written on the blackboard ($1<m<n$) and replace $n$ with $n-m$. Player $A$ makes the first move, then players move alternately. The player who can't make a move loses the game. For which starting numbers is there a winning strategy for player $B$?

bw.2013.0.8.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.8.reviewed_statement: There are $n$ rooms in a sauna, each has unlimited capacity. No room may be attended by a female and a male simultaneously. Moreover, males want to share a room only with males that they don't know and females want to share a room only with females that they know. Find the biggest number $k$ such that any $k$ couples can visit the sauna at the same time, given that two males know each other if and only if their wives know each other.

bw.2013.0.9.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.9.reviewed_statement: In a country there are $2014$ airports, no three of them lying on a line. Two airports are connected by a direct flight if and only if the line passing through them divides the country in two parts, each with $1006$ airports in it. Show that there are no two airports such that one can travel from the first to the second, visiting each of the $2014$ airports exactly once.

bw.2013.0.10.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.10.reviewed_statement: A white equilateral triangle is split into $n^2$ equal smaller triangles by lines that are parallel to the sides of the triangle. Denote a line of triangles to be all triangles that are placed between two adjacent parallel lines that form the grid. In particular, a triangle in a corner is also considered to be a line of triangles. We are to paint all triangles black by a sequence of operations of the following kind: choose a line of triangles that contains at least one white triangle and paint this line black. Find the smallest and largest possible number of operations.

bw.2013.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.11.reviewed_statement: In an acute triangle $ABC$ with $AC>AB$, let $D$ be the projection of $A$ on $BC$, and let $E$ and $F$ be the projections of $D$ on $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. Let $G$ be the intersection point of the lines $AD$ and $EF$. Let $H$ be the second intersection point of the line $AD$ and the circumcircle of triangle $ABC$. Prove that $AG\cdot AH=AD^2$.

bw.2013.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.12.reviewed_statement: A trapezoid $ABCD$ with bases $AB$ and $CD$ is such that the circumcircle of the triangle $BCD$ intersects the line $AD$ in a point $E$, distinct from $A$ and $D$. Prove that the circumcircle of the triangle $ABE$ is tangent to the line $BC$.

bw.2013.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.13.reviewed_statement: All faces of a tetrahedron are right-angled triangles. It is known that three of its edges have the same length $s$. Find the volume of the tetrahedron.

bw.2013.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.14.reviewed_statement: Circles $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of the same radius intersect in two points, one of which is $P$. Denote by $A$ and $B$, respectively, the points diametrically opposite to $P$ on each of $\alpha$ and $\beta$. A third circle of the same radius passes through $P$ and intersects $\alpha$ and $\beta$ in the points $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Show that the line $XY$ is parallel to the line $AB$.

bw.2013.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.15.reviewed_statement: Four circles in a plane have a common centre. Their radii form a strictly increasing arithmetic progression. Prove that there is no square with each vertex lying on a different circle.

bw.2013.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.16.reviewed_statement: We call a positive integer $n$ delightful if there exists an integer $k$, $1<k<n$, such that $$1+2+\cdots+(k-1)=(k+1)+(k+2)+\cdots+n.$$ Does there exist a delightful number $N$ satisfying the inequalities $$2013^{2013}<\frac{N}{2013^{2013}}<2013^{2013}+4\ ?$$

bw.2013.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.17.reviewed_statement: Let $c$ and $n>c$ be positive integers. Mary's teacher writes $n$ positive integers on a blackboard. Is it true that for all $n$ and $c$ Mary can always label the numbers written by the teacher by $a_1, \ldots, a_n$ in such an order that the cyclic product $(a_1-a_2)(a_2-a_3)\cdots(a_{n-1}-a_n)(a_n-a_1)$ would be congruent to either $0$ or $c$ modulo $n$?

bw.2013.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.18.reviewed_statement: Find all pairs $(x,y)$ of integers such that $y^3-1=x^4+x^2$.

bw.2013.0.19.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.19.reviewed_statement: Let $a_0$ be a positive integer and $a_n=5a_{n-1}+4$ for all $n\geq 1$. Can $a_0$ be chosen so that $a_{54}$ is a multiple of $2013$?

bw.2013.0.20.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2013.0.20.reviewed_statement: Find all polynomials $f$ with non-negative integer coefficients such that for all primes $p$ and positive integers $n$ there exist a prime $q$ and a positive integer $m$ such that $f(p^n)=q^m$.

bw.2014.0.1.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.

bw.2014.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_N$ be real numbers satisfying $a_0=a_N=0$ and $$a_{i+1}-2a_i+a_{i-1}=a_i^2\quad\text{for } i=1, 2, \ldots, N-1.$$ Prove that $a_i\leq 0$ for $i=1, 2, \ldots, N-1$.

bw.2014.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.3.reviewed_statement: Positive real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ satisfy $\frac1a+\frac1b+\frac1c=3$. Prove the inequality $$\frac{1}{\sqrt{a^3+b}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{b^3+c}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{c^3+a}}\leq\frac{3}{\sqrt2}.$$

bw.2014.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.4.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f$ defined on all real numbers and taking real values such that $$f\big(f(y)\big)+f(x-y)=f\big(xf(y)-x\big)$$ for all real numbers $x$, $y$.

bw.2014.0.5.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.5.reviewed_statement: Given positive real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ that satisfy the equalities $$a^2+d^2-ad=b^2+c^2+bc\quad\text{and}\quad a^2+b^2=c^2+d^2,$$ find all possible values of the expression $\frac{ab+cd}{ad+bc}$.

bw.2014.0.6.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.6.reviewed_statement: In how many ways can we paint $16$ seats in a row, each red or green, in such a way that the number of consecutive seats painted in the same colour is always odd?

bw.2014.0.7.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.7.reviewed_statement: Let $p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_{30}$ be a permutation of the numbers $1, 2, \ldots, 30$. For how many permutations does the equality $$\sum_{k=1}^{30}|p_k-k|=450$$ hold?

bw.2014.0.8.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.

bw.2014.0.9.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.9.reviewed_statement: What is the least possible number of cells that can be marked on an $n\times n$ board such that for each $m>\frac{n}{2}$ both diagonals of any $m\times m$ sub-board contain a marked cell?

bw.2014.0.10.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.10.reviewed_statement: In a country there are $100$ airports. Super-Air operates direct flights between some pairs of airports (in both directions). The traffic of an airport is the number of airports it has a direct Super-Air connection with. A new company, Concur-Air, establishes a direct flight between two airports if and only if the sum of their traffics is at least $100$. It turns out that there exists a round-trip of Concur-Air flights that lands in every airport exactly once. Show that then there also exists a round-trip of Super-Air flights that lands in every airport exactly once.

bw.2014.0.11.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.11.reviewed_statement: Let $\Gamma$ be the circumcircle of an acute triangle $ABC$. The perpendicular to $AB$ from $C$ meets $AB$ at $D$ and $\Gamma$ again at $E$. The bisector of angle $C$ meets $AB$ at $F$ and $\Gamma$ again at $G$. The line $GD$ meets $\Gamma$ again at $H$ and the line $HF$ meets $\Gamma$ again at $I$. Prove that $AI=EB$.

bw.2014.0.12.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.12.reviewed_statement: Triangle $ABC$ is given. Let $M$ be the midpoint of the segment $AB$ and $T$ be the midpoint of the arc $BC$ not containing $A$ of the circumcircle of $ABC$. The point $K$ inside the triangle $ABC$ is such that $MATK$ is an isosceles trapezoid with $AT\parallel MK$. Show that $AK=KC$.

bw.2014.0.13.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.13.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a square inscribed in a circle $\omega$ and let $P$ be a point on the shorter arc $AB$ of $\omega$. Let $CP\cap BD=R$ and $DP\cap AC=S$. Show that triangles $ARB$ and $DSR$ have equal areas.

bw.2014.0.14.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.14.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral such that the line $BD$ bisects the angle $ABC$. The circumcircle of triangle $ABC$ intersects the sides $AD$ and $CD$ in the points $P$ and $Q$, respectively. The line through $D$ and parallel to $AC$ intersects the lines $BC$ and $BA$ at the points $R$ and $S$, respectively. Prove that the points $P$, $Q$, $R$ and $S$ lie on a common circle.

bw.2014.0.15.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.15.reviewed_statement: The sum of the angles $A$ and $C$ of a convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ is less than $180^\circ$. Prove that $$AB\cdot CD+AD\cdot BC<AC(AB+AD).$$

bw.2014.0.16.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.16.reviewed_statement: Determine whether $712!+1$ is a prime number.

bw.2014.0.17.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.17.reviewed_statement: Do there exist pairwise distinct rational numbers $x$, $y$ and $z$ such that $$\frac{1}{(x-y)^2}+\frac{1}{(y-z)^2}+\frac{1}{(z-x)^2}=2014?$$

bw.2014.0.18.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.18.reviewed_statement: Let $p$ be a prime number, and let $n$ be a positive integer. Find the number of quadruples $(a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)$ with $a_i\in\{0, 1, \ldots, p^n-1\}$ for $i=1, 2, 3, 4$, such that $$p^n\mid(a_1a_2+a_3a_4+1).$$

bw.2014.0.19.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.19.reviewed_statement: Let $m$ and $n$ be relatively prime positive integers. Determine all possible values of $$\gcd\left(2^m-2^n,\ 2^{m^2+mn+n^2}-1\right).$$

bw.2014.0.20.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2014.0.20.reviewed_statement: Consider a sequence of positive integers $a_1, a_2, a_3, \ldots$ such that for $k\geq 2$ we have $$a_{k+1}=\frac{a_k+a_{k-1}}{2015^i},$$ where $2015^i$ is the maximal power of $2015$ that divides $a_k+a_{k-1}$. Prove that if this sequence is periodic then its period is divisible by $3$.

bw.2015.0.1.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.1.reviewed_statement: For $n\geq 2$, an equilateral triangle is divided into $n^2$ congruent smaller equilateral triangles. Determine all ways in which real numbers can be assigned to the $\frac{(n+1)(n+2)}{2}$ vertices so that three such numbers sum to zero whenever the three vertices form a triangle with edges parallel to the sides of the big triangle.

bw.2015.0.2.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.2.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $a_1, \ldots, a_n$ be real numbers satisfying $0\leq a_i\leq 1$ for $i=1, \ldots, n$. Prove the inequality $$(1-a_1^n)(1-a_2^n)\cdots(1-a_n^n)\leq(1-a_1a_2\cdots a_n)^n.$$

bw.2015.0.3.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.3.reviewed_statement: Let $n>1$ be an integer. Find all non-constant real polynomials $P(x)$ satisfying, for any real $x$, the identity $$P(x)P(x^2)P(x^3)\cdots P(x^n)=P\left(x^{\frac{n(n+1)}{2}}\right).$$

bw.2015.0.4.scope: Full statement compared with the official English problem sheet (text layer and page image); figures cropped from the same sheet where present.
bw.2015.0.4.reviewed_statement: A family wears clothes of three colours: red, blue and green, with a separate, identical laundry bin for each colour. At the beginning of the first week, all bins are empty. Each week, the family generates a total of $10$ kg of laundry (the proportion of each colour is subject to variation).
