cps.2009.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2009.2.5.reviewed_statement:
An $n$-tuple of integers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ satisfying the following conditions is given:

(i) $1\le a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_n\le 50$;

(ii) for every $n$-tuple of positive integers $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ there exist a positive integer $m$ and an $n$-tuple of positive integers $c_1,\ldots,c_n$ such that $$m\cdot b_i=c_i^{a_i} \quad\text{for } i=1,\ldots,n.$$

Prove that $n\le 16$ and determine the number of distinct $n$-tuples $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ satisfying the given conditions for $n=16$.
cps.2009.2.5.provenance_note: Translated from the official Slovak report; the Czech report (DML-CZ) agrees.

cps.2009.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2009.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $n\ge 16$ be a positive integer. Consider the set $$G=\bigl\{(x,y) : x,y\in\{1,2,\ldots,n\}\bigr\}$$ consisting of $n^2$ points of the plane. Let $A$ be an arbitrary subset of the set $G$ containing at least $4n\sqrt{n}$ elements. Prove that there exist at least $n^2$ convex quadrilaterals with vertices in $A$ all of whose diagonals pass through one point.
cps.2009.2.6.provenance_note: Translated from the official Slovak report; the Czech report (DML-CZ) agrees.

cps.2010.2.4.reviewed_statement: Find the largest integer $k$ for which the following statement is true: Arbitrary $2010$ non-degenerate triangles are given. We obtain $$\begin{aligned}&b_1\le b_2\le\ldots\le b_{2010} &&\text{for the lengths of the blue sides,}\\ &r_1\le r_2\le\ldots\le r_{2010} &&\text{for the lengths of the red sides,}\\ &w_1\le w_2\le\ldots\le w_{2010} &&\text{for the lengths of the white sides.}\end{aligned}$$ Then there exist at least $k$ indices $j$ such that a non-degenerate triangle with side lengths $b_j$, $r_j$, $w_j$ can be formed.

cps.2012.2.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2012.2.5.reviewed_statement:
The city of Mar del Plata has the shape of a square $WSEN$ and is divided by $2(n+1)$ streets into $n\times n$ blocks, where $n$ is a given even number (streets also run along the perimeter of the square). Each block measures $100\times 100$ metres. All streets in Mar del Plata are one-way, each street has the same direction along its whole length, and adjacent parallel streets always have opposite directions. The street $WS$ is driven in the direction from $W$ to $S$ and the street $WN$ from $W$ to $N$. A street-watering car starts at the point $W$. It wants to get to the point $E$ and water as many streets as possible on the way. What is the length of the longest route it can travel if it does not want to traverse any $100$-metre segment more than once? (The figure shows, for $n=6$, the plan of the city and one of the possible, but not longest, routes of the watering car.)

cps.2015.2.4.reviewed_statement:
A strange calculator has only two buttons, and on each of them some positive two-digit number is written. At the beginning the display of the calculator shows the number $1$. After the button with the number $N$ is pressed, the calculator replaces the currently displayed number $X$ by the number $X\cdot N$ or $X+N$, where multiplication and addition are used alternately (multiplication first). For example, if the number $10$ is on the first button and the number $20$ on the second, then successive presses of the first, the second, the first and once more the first button make the calculator display successively the numbers $1\cdot 10=10$, $10+20=30$, $30\cdot 10=300$ and $300+10=310$. Decide whether there exist values of the two-digit numbers on the buttons of the calculator for which infinitely many numbers ending in

(a) $2015$,

(b) $5813$

can be shown on the display.
cps.2015.2.4.provenance_note: Translated from the Polish camp booklet (the only public official source for 2015). Day split P1-P3 / P4-P6 assumed from the standard two-day format; the booklet does not mark days.

cps.2024.1.2.scope: Official English wording compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2024.1.2.reviewed_statement: For a positive integer $n$, an $n$-configuration is a family of sets $\langle A_{i,j}\rangle_{1\le i,j\le n}$. An $n$-configuration is called sweet if for every pair of indices $(i,j)$ with $1\le i\le n-1$ and $1\le j\le n$ we have $A_{i,j}\subseteq A_{i+1,j}$ and $A_{j,i}\subseteq A_{j,i+1}$. Let $f(n,k)$ denote the number of sweet $n$-configurations such that $A_{n,n}\subseteq\{1,2,\ldots,k\}$. Determine which number is larger: $f(2024,2024^2)$ or $f(2024^2,2024)$.

cps.2024.1.3.scope: Official English wording compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2024.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $ABC$ be a triangle and $D$ a point on its side $BC$. Points $E$, $F$ lie on the lines $AB$, $AC$, respectively, such that $B$ lies between $A$ and $E$ and $BE=BD$ and $C$ lies between $A$ and $F$ and $CF=CD$. Let $P$ be a point such that $D$ is the incenter of triangle $PEF$. Prove that $P$ lies inside the circumcircle $\Omega$ of triangle $ABC$ or on it.

cps.2024.2.4.scope: Official English wording compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2024.2.4.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a convex quadrilateral, such that $AB=BC=CD$. There are points $X$, $Y$ on rays $CA$, $BD$, respectively, such that $BX=CY$. Let $P$, $Q$, $R$, $S$ be the midpoints of segments $BX$, $CY$, $XD$, $YA$, respectively. Prove that points $P$, $Q$, $R$, $S$ lie on a circle.

cps.2024.2.5.scope: Official English wording compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2024.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $\alpha\ne 0$ be a real number. Determine all functions $f\colon\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ such that $$f(x^2+y^2)=f(x-y)f(x+y)+\alpha yf(y)$$ holds for all $x,y\in\mathbb{R}$.

cps.2024.2.6.scope: Official English wording compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2024.2.6.reviewed_statement:
Determine whether there exist infinitely many triples $(a,b,c)$ of positive integers such that $p$ divides $\left\lfloor\left(a+b\sqrt{2024}\right)^p\right\rfloor-c$ for every prime $p$.

Note: $\lfloor x\rfloor$ denotes the largest integer not larger than $x$.

cps.2025.1.1.scope: Official English wording compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2025.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $a,b,c,d$ be nonnegative real numbers for which $a^2+b^2=ac+bd$ holds and $c,d$ are not both zero. Find maximum and minimum value of the expression $$\frac{ad+bc-cd}{c^2+d^2}.$$

cps.2025.1.2.scope: Official English wording compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2025.1.2.reviewed_statement: Let $\{a_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of positive integers such that for every positive integer $n$ $$a_{n+1}=(n+1)(a_n-n+1).$$ In terms of $a_1$, determine the greatest positive integer $k$ such that $\gcd(a_i,a_{i+1})=k$ for some positive integer $i\ge 2$. (Note that $\gcd(x,y)$ denotes the greatest common divisor of integers $x$ and $y$.)

cps.2025.1.3.scope: Official English wording compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2025.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Maryam and Artur play a game on a board, taking turns. At the beginning, the polynomial $XY-1$ is written on the board. Artur is the first to make a move. In each move, the player replaces the polynomial $P(X,Y)$ on the board with one of the following polynomials of their choice:

(a) $X\cdot P(X,Y)$

(b) $Y\cdot P(X,Y)$

(c) $P(X,Y)+a$, where $a\in(-\infty,2025]$ is an arbitrary integer.

The game stops after each player has made $2025$ moves. Let $Q(X,Y)$ be the polynomial on the board after the game ends. Maryam wins if the equation $Q(x,y)=0$ has a finite and odd number of positive integer solutions $(x,y)$. Prove that Maryam can always win the game, no matter how Artur plays.

cps.2025.2.4.scope: Official English wording compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2025.2.4.reviewed_statement:
The plane was divided by vertical and horizontal lines into unit squares. Determine whether it is possible to write integers into cells of this infinite grid so that:

(i) every cell contains exactly one integer

(ii) every integer appears exactly once

(iii) for every two cells $A$ and $B$ sharing exactly one vertex, if they contain integers $a$ and $b$ then at least one of the cells sharing a common side with both $A$ and $B$ contains an integer between $a$ and $b$.

cps.2025.2.5.scope: Official English wording compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2025.2.5.reviewed_statement: We are given an acute triangle $ABC$. Point $D$ lies in the halfplane $AB$ containing $C$ and satisfies $DB\perp AB$ and $\angle ADB=45^\circ+\frac{1}{2}\angle ACB$. Similarly, $E$ lies in the halfplane $AC$ containing $B$ and satisfies $AC\perp EC$ and $\angle AEC=45^\circ+\frac{1}{2}\angle ABC$. Let $F$ be the reflection of $A$ in the midpoint of arc $BAC$ (containing point $A$). Prove that points $A$, $D$, $E$, $F$ are concyclic.

cps.2025.2.6.scope: Official English wording compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2025.2.6.reviewed_statement: Find all functions $f\colon(0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ such that for all $x,y\in(0,\infty)$ it holds that $$f(x+yf(x))=f(x)f(x+y).$$

cps.2026.1.1.scope: Official English wording compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2026.1.1.reviewed_statement: In a sequence $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{100}$ of $100$ mutually different real numbers, we say that an index $i \in \{2, 3, \ldots, 99\}$ is good if $a_1 + \cdots + a_{i-1} = a_{i+1} + \cdots + a_{100}$. What is the largest possible number of good indices?

cps.2026.1.2.scope: Official English wording compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2026.1.2.reviewed_statement: A positive integer $k$ is called divisive if there exist only finitely many quadruples $(x, y, z, w)$ of positive integers satisfying $$x^2 + y^2 + z^2 + w^2 = xyzw \qquad\text{and}\qquad k \nmid x^2 + y^2 + z^2 + w^2.$$ Find all divisive positive integers.

cps.2026.1.3.scope: Official English wording compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2026.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a quadrilateral possessing an incenter $I$. Points $K$ and $L$ are chosen on the segments $IA$ and $IC$, respectively, such that $CK \perp ID$ and $AL \perp IB$. Points $P$ and $Q$ are chosen on the segments $AD$ and $BC$, respectively, such that $\angle AKP = \angle ICD$ and $\angle CLQ = \angle IAB$. Prove that $IP = IQ$.

cps.2026.2.4.scope: Official English wording compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2026.2.4.reviewed_statement: Tom and Jerry play the following game on a $16 \times 16$ chessboard. Jerry starts by selecting some, but not all of the squares, and placing one red pebble on each of the selected squares. Tom then places his one black pebble on an empty square and chooses whether he wants to be the hunter or the prey. After that, Tom and Jerry alternate turns with Jerry starting. In each turn, a player chooses one of his pebbles and moves it to a square sharing an edge with the current square. If such a turn would move the pebble outside of the board, the pebble appears on the other side of the board (i.e. if the pebble is on the left border, it appears in the same row on the right border and similarly for the other cases). If at any point in the game a pebble of the hunter is on the same square as a pebble of the prey, the hunter wins and the game ends. An infinite game is a win for the prey. Which of the two players has a winning strategy?

cps.2026.2.5.scope: Official English wording compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2026.2.5.reviewed_statement: Let $M$ be the midpoint of side $AD$ of a cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$. Points $K$ and $L$ are chosen on the rays $MB$ and $MC$ respectively such that $\angle DAK + \angle ACM = \angle ABM$ and $\angle LDA + \angle MBD = \angle MCD$. Prove that the points $B$, $C$, $K$, and $L$ lie on one circle.

cps.2026.2.6.scope: Official English wording compared visually with the page image; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cps.2026.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer and let $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ be non-zero real numbers such that $$a_1 + \frac{1}{a_2},\quad a_2 + \frac{1}{a_3},\quad \ldots,\quad a_{n-1} + \frac{1}{a_n},\quad a_n + \frac{1}{a_1}$$ are all integers. Prove that $$a_1a_2\ldots a_n + \frac{1}{a_1a_2\ldots a_n}$$ is also an integer.

cps.2000.2.6.reviewed_statement: Every integer is coloured with one of the colours red, blue, green and white. Let $x$ and $y$ be odd integers such that $|x|\ne|y|$. Prove that there exist two integers of the same colour whose difference takes one of the values $x$, $y$, $x+y$ or $x-y$.
cps.2000.2.6.text: Source discrepancy: the Slovak report prints “dve prirodzené čísla” (two positive integers) in the conclusion; the Czech report prints “dvě celá čísla” (two integers), which is followed here.

cps.2001.2.4.reviewed_statement:
Points $A$, $B$ ($A
e B$) are given in the plane. In this plane consider an arbitrary triangle $ABC$ with the property: on its sides $BC$, $CA$ there exist, respectively, points $D$, $E$ for which

(i) $\dfrac{|BD|}{|BC|}=\dfrac{|CE|}{|CA|}=\dfrac{1}{3}$;

(ii) the points $A$, $B$, $D$, $E$ lie (in this order) on one circle.

Determine the set of intersection points of the lines $AD$ and $BE$ for all triangles $ABC$ with the given property.
cps.2001.2.4.text: Source discrepancy (minor): the Slovak report says the points D, E lie “on its sides”, the Czech report “in the interiors of its sides”.

cps.2003.1.1.reviewed_statement: Let $n\ge 2$ be a positive integer. Solve in the real numbers the system of equations $$\begin{aligned}\max\{1,x_1\}&=x_2,\\ \max\{2,x_2\}&=2x_3,\\ &\;\;\vdots\\ \max\{n-1,x_{n-1}\}&=(n-1)x_n,\\ \max\{n,x_n\}&=nx_1.\end{aligned}$$
cps.2003.1.1.text: Editorial correction: both official reports (Slovak and Czech) print the second equation as max{2, x_2} = x_3; the pattern of the system and the official solution (i = max{i, x_i} = i x_{i+1}, unique solution x_1 = ... = x_n = 1) require max{2, x_2} = 2x_3.

cps.2010.2.4.reviewed_statement: Find the largest integer $k$ for which the following statement is true: Arbitrary $2010$ non-degenerate triangles are given. In each triangle the sides are coloured so that one is blue, one is red and one is white. For each colour separately we order the lengths of the sides. We obtain $$\begin{aligned}&b_1\le b_2\le\ldots\le b_{2010} &&\text{for the lengths of the blue sides,}\\ &r_1\le r_2\le\ldots\le r_{2010} &&\text{for the lengths of the red sides,}\\ &w_1\le w_2\le\ldots\le w_{2010} &&\text{for the lengths of the white sides.}\end{aligned}$$ Then there exist at least $k$ indices $j$ such that a non-degenerate triangle with side lengths $b_j$, $r_j$, $w_j$ can be formed.
cps.2010.2.4.text: Source note: The Czech report (DML-CZ) words the conclusion as 'there exist $k$ indices $j$ ... Prove it.' without 'at least'; the Slovak wording with 'at least' is used.

cps.2012.2.5.reviewed_statement:
The city of Mar del Plata has the shape of a square $WSEN$ and is divided by $2(n+1)$ streets into $n\times n$ blocks, where $n$ is a given even number (streets also run along the perimeter of the square). Each block measures $100\times 100$ metres. All streets in Mar del Plata are one-way, each street has the same direction along its whole length, and adjacent parallel streets always have opposite directions. The street $WS$ is driven in the direction from $W$ to $S$ and the street $WN$ from $W$ to $N$. A street-watering car starts at the point $W$. It wants to get to the point $E$ and water as many streets as possible on the way. What is the length of the longest route it can travel if it does not want to traverse any $100$-metre segment more than once? (The figure shows, for $n=6$, the plan of the city and one of the possible, but not longest, routes of the watering car.)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/cps_2012_p5_fig.png
cps.2012.2.5.text: Source note: Slovak report Obr. 50 cropped as the figure. The Slovak text also adds 'See also http://goo.gl/maps/JAzD.' (a short map link, omitted here). The Polish booklet states the problem without the figure and without the figure sentence.

cps.2013.1.1.reviewed_statement: A cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ with $|BC|=|CD|$ is given. Let $\omega$ be the circle with centre $C$ tangent to the diagonal $BD$, and let $I$ be the incentre of the triangle $ABD$. Prove that the line through the point $I$ parallel to $AB$ is tangent to the circle $\omega$.
cps.2013.1.1.text: Source note: The Polish booklet prints Problems 1 and 2 in the opposite order (this problem is No. 2 there); the Slovak order is kept.

cps.2013.1.2.reviewed_statement: Prove that for every real number $x>0$ and every integer $n>0$ $$x^n+\frac{1}{x^n}-2\ge n^2\left(x+\frac{1}{x}-2\right).$$
cps.2013.1.2.text: Source note: The Polish booklet prints Problems 1 and 2 in the opposite order (this problem is No. 1 there); the Slovak order is kept.

cps.2013.2.5.reviewed_statement:
A triangular grid divides an equilateral triangle with side length $n$ into $n^2$ triangular cells (see the figure). Some cells are infected. A cell that is not yet infected becomes infected if it shares a side with at least two already infected cells. For $n=12$, determine the smallest possible number of initially infected cells for which it is possible that after some time all cells of the original triangle are infected.

cps.2014.2.4.reviewed_statement: A triangle $ABC$ is given, and $P$ is the midpoint of the side $AC$. A circle $k$ intersects the segments $AP$, $CP$, $BC$, $AB$ at their interior points $K$, $L$, $M$, $N$, respectively. Let $S$ be the midpoint of $KL$. Suppose that $$2\cdot|AN|\cdot|AB|\cdot|CL|=2\cdot|CM|\cdot|BC|\cdot|AK|=|AC|\cdot|AK|\cdot|CL|.$$ Prove that if $P\ne S$, then the intersection of the lines $KN$ and $ML$ lies on the perpendicular bisector of the segment $PS$.
cps.2014.2.4.text: Source note: The Polish booklet omits the hypothesis $P\ne S$; the Slovak wording is kept.

cps.2016.1.3.reviewed_statement: Let $n$ be a given positive integer. For a finite set $M$ of positive integers and for every $i\in\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$, denote by $s_i$ the number of nonempty subsets of $M$ whose sum of elements leaves remainder $i$ upon division by $n$. We say that the set $M$ is $n$-balanced if $s_0=s_1=\ldots=s_{n-1}$. For example, for $n=5$ and $M=\{1,3,4\}$ we have $s_0=s_1=s_2=1$ and $s_3=s_4=2$, so $M$ is not $5$-balanced. Prove that for every odd positive integer $n$ there exists an $n$-balanced subset of the set $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$.
cps.2016.1.3.text: Source ambiguity: the official Slovak sheet does not say that the required $n$-balanced subset must be nonempty, although the empty set satisfies $s_0=\ldots=s_{n-1}=0$ trivially; the intended subset is evidently nonempty.

cpsj.2012.2.7.reviewed_statement:

(b) Determine the set of midpoints $S$ of the segments $FG$ corresponding to all admissible positions of the point $C$.

cpsj.2015.2.7.reviewed_statement:

b) What is the smallest number of queens that can be placed on the chessboard so that all $60$ squares are attacked by them?

cpsj.2019.2.10.reviewed_statement: A regular $360$-gon $A_1A_2\ldots A_{360}$ with centre $S$ is given. For each of the triangles $A_1A_{50}A_{68}$ and $A_1A_{50}A_{69}$ decide whether its images under $120$ suitable rotations about the centre $S$ can have (as triangles) all $360$ points $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_{360}$ as their vertices.

cpsj.2019.2.11.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2019.2.11.reviewed_statement:
A cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$ is given. Points $K$, $L$, $M$, $N$ lie on the sides $AB$, $BC$, $CD$, $DA$, respectively, such that
$$|\angle ADK|=|\angle BCK|,\qquad |\angle BAL|=|\angle CDL|,$$
$$|\angle CBM|=|\angle DAM|,\qquad |\angle DCN|=|\angle ABN|.$$
Prove that the lines $KM$ and $LN$ are perpendicular to each other.

cpsj.2021.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2021.1.1.reviewed_statement:
A $2\times 2$ table is given in which every square contains a positive integer. If we add the product of the numbers in the first column, the product of the numbers in the second column, the product of the numbers in the first row and the product of the numbers in the second row, we obtain $2021$.

a) Determine the possible values of the sum of the four numbers in the table.

b) Find the number of different tables satisfying the given conditions which contain four pairwise distinct numbers.

cpsj.2021.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2021.1.2.reviewed_statement: An acute triangle $ABC$ is given. Denote by $D$ and $E$ the orthogonal projections of the points $B$ and $C$, respectively, onto the bisector of the exterior angle $BAC$. Let $F$ be the intersection point of the lines $BE$ and $CD$. Prove that the lines $AF$ and $DE$ are perpendicular.

cpsj.2021.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2021.1.3.reviewed_statement:
A cross is a figure consisting of $6$ unit squares shown in the figure (and any figure obtained from it by a rotation). Determine the largest number of crosses that can be cut out of a $6\times 11$ sheet of paper divided into unit squares (in such a way that every cross consists of six such squares).

cpsj.2021.1.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2021.1.4.reviewed_statement:
Determine the smallest value taken by the expression
$$x^4+y^4-x^2y-xy^2$$
for positive numbers $x$ and $y$ satisfying the inequality $x+y\leqslant 1$.

cpsj.2021.1.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2021.1.5.reviewed_statement: A regular heptagon $ABCDEFG$ is given. The lines $AB$ and $CE$ intersect at a point $P$. Determine the measure of the angle $PDG$.

cpsj.2021.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2021.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $ABCD$ be a trapezoid with bases $AB$ and $CD$ satisfying $|AB|>|CD|$. Denote by $M$ the midpoint of the segment $AB$. Let a point $P$ lie inside $ABCD$ with $|AD|=|PC|$ and $|BC|=|PD|$. Prove that if $|\angle CMD|=90^\circ$, then the quadrilaterals $AMPD$ and $BMPC$ have the same area.

cpsj.2021.2.7.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2021.2.7.reviewed_statement:
Numbers $x_i\in\{-1,1\}$ for $i=1,2,\ldots,n$ are given, satisfying
$$x_1x_2+x_2x_3+\ldots+x_{n-1}x_n+x_nx_1=0.$$
Prove that $n$ is divisible by $4$.

cpsj.2021.2.8.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2021.2.8.reviewed_statement:
Determine the number of pairs $(a,b)$ of positive integers with the property that the greatest common divisor of the numbers $a$ and $b$ is equal to
$$1\cdot 2\cdot 3\cdot\ldots\cdot 50,$$
and the least common multiple of the numbers $a$ and $b$ is equal to
$$1^2\cdot 2^2\cdot 3^2\cdot\ldots\cdot 50^2.$$

cpsj.2021.2.9.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2021.2.9.reviewed_statement:
Determine the smallest positive integer $n$ with the property that in the set
$$\{70,71,72,\ldots,70+n\}$$
one can choose two distinct numbers whose product is the square of an integer.

cpsj.2021.2.10.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2021.2.10.reviewed_statement:
Find all triples of real numbers $(x,y,z)$ satisfying the system of equations
$$\frac{x}{y}+\frac{y}{z}+\frac{z}{x}=\frac{x}{z}+\frac{z}{y}+\frac{y}{x},$$
$$x^2+y^2+z^2=xy+yz+zx+4.$$

cpsj.2021.2.11.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2021.2.11.reviewed_statement:
Let $s(n)$ denote the digit sum of a positive integer $n$. Using six distinct digits, we formed three two-digit numbers $p$, $q$, $r$ such that
$$p\cdot q\cdot s(r)=p\cdot s(q)\cdot r=s(p)\cdot q\cdot r.$$
Find all such numbers $p$, $q$, $r$.

cpsj.2022.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2022.1.1.reviewed_statement:
Let $n\geqslant 3$. Suppose that $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ are $n$ pairwise distinct real numbers. Determine, in terms of $n$, the smallest possible number of distinct values taken by the following $n$ numbers:
$$a_1+a_2,\quad a_2+a_3,\quad \ldots,\quad a_{n-1}+a_n,\quad a_n+a_1.$$

cpsj.2022.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2022.1.2.reviewed_statement:
Solve in integers the following system of equations:
$$\begin{cases} x^2=yz+1,\\ y^2=zx+1,\\ z^2=xy+1.\end{cases}$$

cpsj.2022.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2022.1.3.reviewed_statement:
A convex pentagon $ABCDE$ is given in which
$$\angle A=60^\circ,\quad \angle B=100^\circ,\quad \angle C=140^\circ.$$
Prove that this pentagon can be placed in a disc of radius $\frac{2}{3}AD$.

cpsj.2022.1.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2022.1.4.reviewed_statement:
Let $a$, $b$ be positive integers with the property that $\frac{a}{b}>\sqrt{2}$. Prove that
$$\frac{a}{b}-\frac{1}{2ab}>\sqrt{2}.$$

cpsj.2022.1.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2022.1.5.reviewed_statement: An integer $n\geqslant 1$ is called good if the following property holds: if a positive integer is divisible by each of the nine numbers $n+1$, $n+2$, $\ldots$, $n+9$, then it is also divisible by the number $n+10$. How many good integers $n\geqslant 1$ are there?

cpsj.2022.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2022.2.6.reviewed_statement: Determine the largest possible value of the expression $ab+bc+2ac$ for non-negative real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ whose sum is $1$.

cpsj.2022.2.7.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2022.2.7.reviewed_statement:
The number $2022$ is written on the board. In each step we replace one of the digits $2$ by the number $2022$. For example
$$2022\ \Rightarrow\ 20\underline{2022}2\ \Rightarrow\ 20202\underline{2022}2\ \Rightarrow\ \ldots$$
After how many steps can a number divisible by $22$ be written on the board? Determine all possibilities.

cpsj.2022.2.8.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2022.2.8.reviewed_statement: Points $D$, $E$, $F$ lie on the sides $BC$, $CA$, $AB$ of a triangle $ABC$, respectively, in such a way that $FB=BD$, $DC=CE$, and the lines $EF$ and $BC$ are parallel. The tangent to the circle circumscribed about the triangle $DEF$ at the point $F$ meets the segment $AD$ at a point $P$. The perpendicular bisector of the segment $EF$ meets the segment $AC$ at a point $Q$. Prove that the lines $PQ$ and $BC$ are parallel.

cpsj.2022.2.9.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2022.2.9.reviewed_statement:
Find all triples $(a,b,c)$ of integers which satisfy the equations
$$a+b=c\quad\text{and}\quad a^2+b^3=c^2.$$

cpsj.2022.2.10.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2022.2.10.reviewed_statement: A regular nonagon $A_1A_2A_3A_4A_5A_6A_7A_8A_9$ with side length $1$ is given. The diagonals $A_3A_7$ and $A_4A_8$ intersect at a point $P$. Find the length of the segment $PA_1$.

cpsj.2022.2.11.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2022.2.11.reviewed_statement:
Determine all integers $n\ge 4$ with the following property: every square of an $n\times n$ table can be coloured white or black in such a way that every square of this table has the same colour as exactly two of its neighbouring squares. (Squares are neighbouring if they have exactly one common side.)

How many different colourings of the squares of a $6\times 6$ table satisfy the above conditions?

cpsj.2023.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2023.1.1.reviewed_statement: A triangle $ABC$ with $BC=2\cdot AC$ is given. Point $M$ is the midpoint of the side $BC$, and point $D$ lies on the segment $AB$ with $AD=2\cdot BD$. Prove that the lines $AM$ and $MD$ are perpendicular.

cpsj.2023.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2023.1.2.reviewed_statement: For a positive integer $n$ denote by $d(n)$ the number of positive divisors of $n$. Determine all positive integers $n$ for which $d(n)$ is the second largest divisor of $n$.

cpsj.2023.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2023.1.3.reviewed_statement: An acute triangle $ABC$ is given. A point $P$ is inside this triangle and lies on the bisector of the angle $BAC$. Suppose that the orthocentre $H$ of the triangle $ABP$ lies inside the triangle $ABC$. Let $Q$ be the intersection of the line $AP$ and the line perpendicular to $AC$ passing through $H$. Prove that $Q$ is the point symmetric to $P$ with respect to the line $BH$.

cpsj.2023.1.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2023.1.4.reviewed_statement:
Every square of an $n\times n$ board has been coloured either red or blue, in such a way that the following conditions are satisfied:

- if a row and a column contain the same number of red squares, then the square at their intersection is red;

- if a row and a column contain different numbers of red squares, then the square at their intersection is blue.

Prove that the total number of blue squares is even.

cpsj.2023.1.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2023.1.5.reviewed_statement: Bartek patiently performs operations on fractions. In each move he adds to the current result its reciprocal, obtaining a new result. Bartek starts with the number $1$: after the first move he therefore obtains the result $2$, after the second move the result $\frac{5}{2}$, after the third $\frac{29}{10}$, etc. After $300$ moves Bartek obtained the result $x$. Determine the largest integer not greater than $x$.

cpsj.2023.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2023.2.6.reviewed_statement: Denote by $S(n)$ the sum of all digits of a positive integer $n$. Determine all positive integers $n$ for which both numbers $n+S(n)$ and $n-S(n)$ are squares of non-zero integers.

cpsj.2023.2.7.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2023.2.7.reviewed_statement:
The numbers $1, 2, \ldots, 2023$ are written on the board in this order. We may repeatedly perform the following operation on them: we choose any odd number of consecutive numbers and write these numbers in reverse order. How many different orders of these $2023$ numbers can we obtain in this way?

Example: If we start with just the numbers $1,2,3,4,5,6$, we can perform the following steps
$$\mathbf{1},\mathbf{2},\mathbf{3},4,5,6\to 3,\mathbf{2},\mathbf{1},\mathbf{4},\mathbf{5},\mathbf{6}\to 3,6,\mathbf{5},\mathbf{4},\mathbf{1},2\to 3,6,1,4,5,2\to\ldots$$

cpsj.2023.2.9.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2023.2.9.reviewed_statement: In a triangle $ABC$ the points $M$ and $N$ are the midpoints of the sides $AB$ and $AC$, respectively. The bisectors of the interior angles $ABC$ and $BCA$ meet the line $MN$ at points $P$ and $Q$, respectively. Let $p$ be the tangent to the circle circumscribed about the triangle $AMP$ passing through the point $P$, and let $q$ be the tangent to the circle circumscribed about the triangle $ANQ$ passing through the point $Q$. Prove that the lines $p$ and $q$ intersect on the line $BC$.

cpsj.2023.2.10.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.

cpsj.2023.2.11.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2023.2.11.reviewed_statement: A rectangle $ABCD$ is given. Points $E$ and $F$ lie on the sides $BC$ and $CD$, respectively, so that the area of each of the triangles $ABE$, $ECF$, $FDA$ is equal to $1$. Determine the area of the triangle $AEF$.

cpsj.2024.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2024.1.1.reviewed_statement:
Initially the numbers $1$ and $2$ are written on the board. A move consists of choosing a positive real number $x$ and replacing the pair $(a,b)$ of numbers written on the board by the pair
$$\left(a+\frac{x}{b},\,b+\frac{x}{a}\right).$$
Is it possible (in finitely many moves) to reach a situation in which the two numbers written on the board are $2$ and $3$?

cpsj.2024.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2024.1.2.reviewed_statement: How many non-empty subsets of the set $\{1,2,3,4,\ldots,11\}$ have the property that the product of all elements of the subset is the cube of an integer?

cpsj.2024.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2024.1.3.reviewed_statement: A convex quadrilateral $ABCD$ is given in which $AB=BD=DC$ and $AB\perp BD\perp DC$. Point $M$ is the midpoint of the side $BC$. Prove that $\angle BAM+\angle DCA=45^\circ$.

cpsj.2024.1.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2024.1.4.reviewed_statement:
Integers $a$, $b$, $c$ satisfy the conditions $a+b+c=1$ and $ab+bc+ca<abc$. Prove that
$$ab+bc+ca<2abc.$$

cpsj.2024.1.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2024.1.5.reviewed_statement: For a positive integer $n$ denote by $S(n)$ the sum of the digits in the decimal representation of the number $n$. Determine the smallest positive integer $n$ for which the equality $4\cdot S(n)=3\cdot S(2n)$ holds.

cpsj.2024.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2024.2.6.reviewed_statement: Let $G$ be the centroid of a triangle $ABC$. Let $D$ be the fourth vertex of the parallelogram $AGDB$. Prove that $BG\parallel CD$.

cpsj.2024.2.7.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2024.2.7.reviewed_statement:
Among the triples $(a,b,c)$ of positive integers satisfying
$$\left(a+14\sqrt{3}\right)\left(b-14c\sqrt{3}\right)=2024$$
determine the one with the largest value of $a$.

cpsj.2024.2.8.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2024.2.8.reviewed_statement: Determine the measures of the interior angles in all isosceles triangles which can be divided into two isosceles triangles with disjoint interiors.

cpsj.2024.2.9.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2024.2.9.reviewed_statement:
How many positive integers $n$ less than $2024$ are divisible by $\lfloor\sqrt{n}\rfloor-1$? The symbol $\lfloor x\rfloor$ denotes the largest integer not greater than $x$.

For example, $n=8$ satisfies the given condition, since $8$ is divisible by $\lfloor\sqrt{8}\rfloor-1=2-1=1$, but $n=9$ does not satisfy it, since $9$ is not divisible by $\lfloor\sqrt{9}\rfloor-1=2$.

cpsj.2024.2.10.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2024.2.10.reviewed_statement: Does there exist an integer $n\ge 1$ such that when the digits of the number $2^n$, written in the decimal system, are written in reverse order, we obtain a different integer power of two?

cpsj.2024.2.11.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2024.2.11.reviewed_statement: Every cell of a rectangular table contains a positive integer. For every cell of the table, the number in it is equal to the total number of distinct values in the cells which are in the same row or column as it (including itself). Find all tables with this property.

cpsj.2025.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2025.1.1.reviewed_statement:
Determine all primes $p$ for which the number
$$p^3+p^2+p+1$$
can be written as the product of two distinct primes.

cpsj.2025.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2025.1.2.reviewed_statement: Determine all triangles which can be divided into congruent parts, each of which is a right isosceles triangle whose legs have length $1$.

cpsj.2025.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2025.1.3.reviewed_statement: A triangle $ABC$ with $\angle ACB=60^\circ$ is given. Points $D$, $E$ lie on the sides $BC$, $AC$ of this triangle, respectively. Points $K$, $L$ are such that the triangles $ADK$ and $BEL$ are equilateral, where the points $A$ and $L$ lie on opposite sides of the line $BE$, and the points $B$ and $K$ lie on opposite sides of the line $AD$. Prove that $AE+BD=KL$.

cpsj.2025.1.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2025.1.4.reviewed_statement: Initially three non-negative integers are written on the board. In a single step we replace the triple $a$, $b$, $c$ of numbers written on the board by the sums $a+b$, $b+c$, $c+a$. Determine the largest number of steps after which the number $111$ can appear on the board.

cpsj.2025.1.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2025.1.5.reviewed_statement:
Prove that for every integer $n\geqslant 1$ the number
$$A_n=\frac{1}{n+1}-\frac{2}{n+2}+\frac{3}{n+3}-\frac{4}{n+4}+\ldots+\frac{2n-1}{3n-1}$$
is greater than $\frac{1}{3}$.

cpsj.2025.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2025.2.6.reviewed_statement: Consider the following operation on a two-digit number: first we multiply its digits, then we compute the square of its last digit, and we write these two results one after the other in this order (e.g. for the number $27$ we compute $14$ and $49$, from which we obtain $1449$). A four-digit number is called showy if its square root is a two-digit number and the operation applied to this square root produces the original four-digit number. Determine all showy numbers.

cpsj.2025.2.7.scope: English translation compared with the official Czech text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2025.2.7.reviewed_statement:
For a rectangular sheet of paper $ABCD$ we have $|AB|:|BC|=3:1$. On its sides $AB$ and $CD$ lie points $M$ and $N$, respectively, such that $|AM|:|AD|=|CN|:|CB|=1:2$. We fold the sheet so that the point $D$ coincides with the point $M$. Then we fold it again, bringing the point $B$ onto the point $N$. A hexagon $APRCQS$ is formed, as in the figure. Prove that this hexagon can be divided by $6$ lines into right triangles.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/national-olympiads-bank/main/images/cpsj_2025_p7_fig.png

cpsj.2025.2.8.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2025.2.8.reviewed_statement: Let $n\geqslant 3$ be an integer. In the plane $2n$ points are marked, no three of which lie on one line. Among these points, $n$ points are coloured red and the remaining $n$ are coloured blue (each point has exactly one colour). Determine, in terms of $n$, the largest positive integer $k$ with the following property: it is always possible (regardless of which points were chosen and how they were coloured) to draw a $k$-gon with red vertices and a $k$-gon with blue vertices in such a way that they have no common points.

cpsj.2025.2.9.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2025.2.9.reviewed_statement:
Can one always find, among any $21$ pairwise distinct real numbers, two distinct numbers $x$, $y$ with the property that
$$20|x-y|<(x+1)(y+1)?$$

cpsj.2025.2.10.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2025.2.10.reviewed_statement:
Let $\{a_n\}_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of positive real numbers such that for all positive integers $n$
$$a_{n+1}=a_n+\frac{1}{a_n}.$$
Find the largest integer $N$ such that exactly $N$ terms of the sequence are integers for some real $a_1$.

cpsj.2025.2.11.scope: English translation compared with the official Slovak text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2025.2.11.reviewed_statement:
Let $n\ge 1$ be an integer. A sequence of $n$ arrows, each of which points to the left ($\leftarrow$) or to the right ($\rightarrow$), is called interesting if no two arrows point at the same number of arrows. Determine the number of all interesting sequences of $n$ arrows.

Example: For $n=5$, in the sequence $\rightarrow\leftarrow\leftarrow\rightarrow\rightarrow$ the numbers of arrows at which the individual arrows point are $4, 1, 2, 1, 0$ in turn. Therefore this sequence is not interesting (since the number $1$ appeared twice).

cpsj.2026.1.1.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2026.1.1.reviewed_statement: In how many ways can the set $\{1,2,\ldots,2n\}$ be divided into $n$ pairs in such a way that the sum of the numbers in each pair is one greater than some power of $2$?

cpsj.2026.1.2.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2026.1.2.reviewed_statement:
In a regular dodecagon $ABCDEFGHIJKL$ the diagonals $AH$ and $EK$ intersect at a point $P$. Prove that
$$AC+KP=AE.$$

cpsj.2026.1.3.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2026.1.3.reviewed_statement:
Real numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ have the property that the fractions
$$\frac{bc+1}{a},\quad \frac{ca+1}{b},\quad \frac{ab+1}{c}$$
have the same value. Which real numbers can this common value be?

cpsj.2026.1.4.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2026.1.4.reviewed_statement: In every square cell of a $100\times 100$ board we draw $0$, $1$ or $2$ diagonals. Determine the largest number of diagonals that can be drawn so that no two of them have a common endpoint.

cpsj.2026.1.5.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2026.1.5.reviewed_statement: A right triangle $ABC$ with the right angle at the vertex $A$ is given. Let $D$ be the intersection point of the bisector of the angle $\angle BAC$ with the side $BC$. Assume that the length of the segment $AD$ is a rational number. What is the largest possible number of sides of the triangle $ABC$ whose lengths are rational numbers?

cpsj.2026.2.6.scope: English translation compared with the official Polish text and visually inspected formulas; not an independent mathematical or human certification.
cpsj.2026.2.6.reviewed_statement:
Positive integers $a$, $b$, $c$ satisfy the condition

USA-AMC10-problems.json.coverage_notes: AMC 10 2000–2025: 2000–2001 one paper; from 2002 AMC 10A and 10B (papers 1 and 2), 2021 also the Fall AMC 10A/10B (papers 3 and 4); 25 problems each, 1,300 statements. MISSING: the 2002 AMC 10P (no numbered copy reachable). The 2026 contests had not been held. Problems © Mathematical Association of America. SECONDARY source: text from public copies of the AoPS wiki (CreativeMath, sudhanshu, edev2000), the identical AMC 12 problem's wiki text where no AMC 10 copy exists, and LIVE (Po-Shen Loh) text for 67 problems with no wiki copy (mostly 2024–2025); every statement cross-checked with LIVE, differences recorded in docs/amc10-2026-10-15.json. Figures drawn by the bank in Asymptote. No source badges. See docs/usa-amc-2026-10-15.md.
